player carries a revolver and a clapperboard. Snapping the clapperboard freezes the scene for 4 s: enemies, their
shots and machines stop, the player keeps moving, and shots fired in the freeze hang in the air and fly when the
scene resumes ("CUT!" on the snap, "ACTION!" on the resume).

and the music into the game. Do A first and commit it on its own.

## Part A: five small changes

Every number goes in `SupercutTuning.h` with a comment, like the ones there. Each change gets a test where a test
can show it.

1. **A gate gives health back.** Walking through a room's gate gives the player 25 health, capped at full health.
   Not on the last room's gate. Today nothing heals, and a sloppy first-time player is dead by room 3.
2. **The Rusher rests longer after a lunge that lands.** After a hit: 1.8 s before it can crouch again. After a
   miss it stays 0.9 s. Today a player who stands still loses 35 health every 1.37 s.
3. **Control in the air.** Today a jump with no run-up covers 223 cm and a running jump about 528 cm, so the order
   of two key presses decides whether the player clears a 200 cm fire strip. Raise the character's air control
   until a player who presses jump and then forward at once, from standing at the edge, lands past a 200 cm strip.
   Check the engine source for what the setting does. Report the value and the measured distances for a standing
   jump with forward held from the start, a standing jump with forward pressed 0.1 s after the jump, and a running
   jump. Keep the running jump under 600 cm.
4. **The death line names what killed.** Today it says `PLAYER dies (shot)` for a Rusher's lunge. Say `lunge`,
   `shot`, `marksman shot`, or the hazard's name.
5. **A `fire` step that fires nothing says so.** A script `fire` step sent before the gun is ready is logged as
   done but fires nothing. Log a line that says it was refused and why.

Also fix `Tools\run_demo.ps1`: it passes the script, picture and log paths unquoted, so a path with a space fails
with exit code 3 and no log. Check how the game reads those switches before you choose the quoting, and prove it
with a script path that has a space in it.

After Part A: all tests pass, and the five fight rooms still play through. Run `Script\fight5.txt` with
`-Run fight5 -Seed 1 -FixedFps 240` (uncooked or packaged). Before your changes it ends
`RUN wrapped: takes 1, time 76.4 s, shots 41, freezes 11, kills 17` with health 100. If the air control change
moves the player in room 4 (it jumps to a rock and back) and the script fails, fix the script's steps, not the
room, and say what you changed. Commit Part A.

## Part B: sound and music in the game

The two handoffs say how each file is meant to be used: which sounds are flat and which sit on an object, what
happens to each at the freeze, the timing offsets, loop fades, and how the music stems line up. Follow them. Where
a handoff offers a choice, its author's pick is the default. What I add:

**What a player must hear, in order of weight.**

1. The clapperboard. The snap is the loudest, clearest event in the game. On the snap the music stops dead (5 ms
   fade), the stage ambience gives way to the frozen bed, and everything the frozen world was doing goes quiet as
   the sound handoff's table says. On the resume, `freeze_out` lands its hit on the frame the scene resumes and the
   music comes back from the start of the bar it was cut in. This contrast is the game's theme. If one thing in
   this lane is right, it is this.
2. Every enemy's tell and attack, on the enemy, in step with what the enemy shows: Grunt wind-up and shot, Rusher
   crouch, run and lunge, Marksman aim, lock and shot, enemy shots in flight, hits, and the enemy's end.
3. The player's own actions: revolver shot, empty click, reload, steps, jump, land, getting hurt, dying, a shot
   hanging in a freeze, the release of hanging shots.
4. The world: machines and hazards, the puzzle pieces (door, plates, switch, glyphs, dropper crates, refill pad),
   the film can, the gate, the slate at a room's start.
5. Screens: the upgrade screen, the death screen, the wrap screen.

Use every sound in the table that has an event in the game today. For a sound with no event yet, list it in your
report and do not invent an event for it.

**Music.** Fight rooms play the four action stems, started in sync. The heat stem comes in when 3 or more enemies
are alive or the player was hurt in the last 4 s, as the music handoff describes. Rooms with no enemies play
`mx_puzzle`. The upgrade screen plays `mx_between`. `mx_take_start` at the start of a take, `mx_room_clear` when the
last enemy of a room dies. `mx_title` has no screen yet: leave it out and say so. Cues change on a bar line, as the
handoff says. Start from the handoff's suggested volumes.

**How the files get into the game.** Your choice, with these limits: nothing is made by hand in the editor (a
script in `Tools\` makes every asset, and running it again gives the same result), the packaged game must carry the
sounds, and the looping music must loop without a bump (the music handoff's note on import settings). Check every
engine class, node and setting you use against the 5.9 source in `D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Source`. Do not trust a
remembered name.

**One master volume and one music volume**, each a number from 0 to 1 that code can set at any time, default 1.
A settings menu will use them later. No menu in this lane.

**A log line for every sound started and stopped**, in its own log category so it can be turned off:
the sound's name, flat or placed, and for a placed sound the distance to the player.

## How you prove it

1. Tests: all old tests pass, plus new ones for what can be tested without ears (the right sound is asked for on
   each event, the music state on freeze and resume, the bar the music resumes from, the heat rule, the volumes).
2. A recording of the game's own sound output from a scripted run. Find the engine's way to record the master
   output to a WAV (check the source; do not guess the name) and add a switch for it. Record at real speed: for
   this run leave `-FixedFps` out, because with a fixed step the game does not run in real time and the recording
   would not match what a player hears. Record at least: the fight demo (`Script\mixed.txt` or a fight room) with
   two freezes in it, one puzzle room, and one upgrade screen.
3. Measure those recordings with Python (`Audio\src\measure.py` has loudness and peak code): in the 100 ms after
   each snap the music stems are gone (show the level before and after); the snap's loudest 100 ms against the

   clipping); the music loop join has no bump (record 30 s of a fight room standing still and look at the join at
   26.67 s). Put spectrogram pictures of a freeze and a resume in your lane folder.
4. A packaged run: the packaged game plays the same script with the same sound log lines.
5. Frame rate: report frames per second in the fight demo before and after your work.

## The owner's pitch (13 Nov, 06:03, word for word)

> a roguelite puzzle FPS game, like [another game] X [another game] X [another game].
> you have guns and a clapperboard with limited charges. every time you use your clapperboard, you
> can freeze time for X amount of seconds, allowing you to traverse without the fear of the enemies
> attacking you for the time being. there are light puzzle mechanics like [another game] as well, so not
> every level is just shooting enemies and freezing time to make that easier. puzzles like stopping
> time so the giant wind turbine gets stopped, so you can get through, or glyphs that only show up in
> frozen time, which you need to unlock a doorway. nothing too complex puzzle wise.

Those three games name a genre mix: run-based shooting, time as a tool, small physical puzzles.
Nothing of theirs is copied: no names, characters, levels, art, sound or screen look.

## The fantasy in one sentence

You are the director on a set that fights back: snap the clapperboard, the scene stops, you walk
through it and set up the shot, then it all plays out.

## The clapperboard

Numbers are starting values. They live in one tunables struct so a change is one line.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Charges | 3 |
| Freeze length | 4.0 s |
| End a freeze early | press the clapperboard again |
| Refill | full on entering a room; a film can pickup gives +1 `[pick]` |

While time is frozen:

- Enemies, enemy shots, moving machines and hazards stop where they are. The player moves and
  looks at full speed.
- Nothing frozen can hurt the player. A frozen enemy shot is harmless to touch.
- The player can fire. Each shot leaves the gun, travels about 1 m and hangs in the air. When time
  resumes, every hanging shot flies at once. `[pick]` This is what makes the freeze a setup tool
  and not a pause button: stop the scene, place five shots, walk to cover, let it roll.
- Some things exist only in frozen time (glyphs), and some frozen things can be stood on.

## Guns

Player shots are fast visible projectiles, never instant hits, so they can hang in frozen time.

#include "SupercutTime.h"
#include "Supercut.h"
#include "SupercutTuning.h"
#include "Engine/World.h"
#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

USupercutTime& USupercutTime::Get(const UObject* WorldContext)
{
	check(WorldContext);
	UWorld* World = WorldContext->GetWorld();
	checkf(World, TEXT("USupercutTime::Get: %s has no world"), *WorldContext->GetName());
	USupercutTime* Time = World->GetSubsystem<USupercutTime>();
	checkf(Time, TEXT("USupercutTime::Get: world %s has no time system"), *World->GetName());
	return *Time;
}

void USupercutTime::Initialize(FSubsystemCollectionBase& Collection)
{
	Super::Initialize(Collection);
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	FreezeLength = Tuning.FreezeSeconds;
	MaxCharges = Tuning.Charges;
	Charges = MaxCharges;
}

void USupercutTime::SetRules(float InFreezeLength, int32 InMaxCharges)
{
	check(InFreezeLength > 0.f && InMaxCharges > 0);
	FreezeLength = InFreezeLength;
	MaxCharges = InMaxCharges;
	Charges = FMath::Min(Charges, MaxCharges);
}

void USupercutTime::RefillCharges()
{
	Charges = MaxCharges;
}

bool USupercutTime::AddCharge()
{
	if (Charges >= MaxCharges)
	{
		return false;
	}
	++Charges;
	SinceChargeGained = 0.f;
	return true;
}

void USupercutTime::EndScene()
{
	if (bFrozen)
	{
		SetFrozen(false, TEXT("the room ended"));
		// A room change is not a change the HUD stamps: no "ACTION!" over the next room's first second.
		SinceChange = 1000.f;
	}
	SceneActors.Reset();
	HeldAt.Reset();
}

int32 USupercutTime::CountSceneActors() const
{
	int32 Count = 0;
	for (const TWeakObjectPtr<AActor>& Actor : SceneActors)
	{
		Count += Actor.IsValid() ? 1 : 0;
	}
	return Count;
}

TStatId USupercutTime::GetStatId() const
{
	RETURN_QUICK_DECLARE_CYCLE_STAT(USupercutTime, STATGROUP_Tickables);
}

void USupercutTime::Tick(float DeltaTime)
{
	Super::Tick(DeltaTime);
	SinceChange += DeltaTime;
	SinceChargeGained += DeltaTime;

	// The frame a freeze starts on is not counted, so the scene gets the full length.
	if (bFrozen && GFrameCounter != FreezeStartFrame)
	{
		Remaining -= DeltaTime;
		if (Remaining <= 0.f)
		{
			SetFrozen(false, TEXT("timer ran out"));
		}
	}
}

	}

	Lunge,    // a straight dash along the direction fixed at the end of the windup
	Recover,  // stands still after a lunge

void ASupercutGrunt::TickCombat(float DeltaSeconds, AActor* TargetActor)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	const FVector There = TargetActor->GetActorLocation();
	FVector Flat = There - Here;
	Flat.Z = 0.f;
	const float Distance = Flat.Size();
	const FVector ToTarget = Flat.GetSafeNormal();

	// Can it see the player? A line from its head to the player's middle, stopped by walls and cover.
	const bool bSees = CanSee(TargetActor, Tuning.GruntSightRange, 70.f);

	if (bSees)
	{
		TurnTowards(There, Tuning.GruntTurnRate, DeltaSeconds);

		// Keep the distance, and step sideways.
		StrafeClock += DeltaSeconds;
		if (StrafeClock >= Tuning.GruntStrafeSeconds)
		{
			StrafeClock = 0.f;
			StrafeSign = -StrafeSign;
		}
		float Radial = 0.f;
		if (Distance < Tuning.GruntMinRange)
		{
			Radial = -1.f;
		}
		else if (Distance > Tuning.GruntMaxRange)
		{
			Radial = 1.f;
		}
		const FVector Side(-ToTarget.Y, ToTarget.X, 0.f);
		const FVector Wish = (ToTarget * Radial + Side * (0.7f * StrafeSign)).GetSafeNormal();
		FVector Next = Here + Wish * (Tuning.GruntMoveSpeed * DeltaSeconds);
		if (bHasHome)
		{
			const FVector2D Clamped = ClampToHome(Next);
			if (!FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Clamped.X, Next.X) || !FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Clamped.Y, Next.Y))
			{
				// At the edge of its area: turn the sidestep around.
				StrafeSign = -StrafeSign;
				StrafeClock = 0.f;
			}
			Next.X = Clamped.X;
			Next.Y = Clamped.Y;
		}
		FHitResult Hit;
		SetActorLocation(Next, true, &Hit);
		if (Hit.bBlockingHit)
		{
			StrafeSign = -StrafeSign;
			StrafeClock = 0.f;
		}
	}

	// Fire on a steady clock. The clock waits at the start of the windup while the player is out of sight.
	const float WindupStart = Tuning.GruntFireInterval - Tuning.GruntWindup;
	FireClock += DeltaSeconds;
	if (!bSees)
	{
		FireClock = FMath::Min(FireClock, WindupStart);
	}
	const float Windup = FMath::Clamp((FireClock - WindupStart) / Tuning.GruntWindup, 0.f, 1.f);
	Muzzle->SetRelativeScale3D(FVector(8.f + 26.f * Windup) / 100.0);
	MuzzleMaterial->SetScalarParameterValue(TEXT("Strength"), 1.f + 60.f * Windup);
	if (FireClock >= Tuning.GruntFireInterval)
	{
		FireClock = 0.f;
		Fire(TargetActor);
	}
}

void ASupercutPlates::HitPlate(int32 Plate)
{
	if (bSolved)
	{
		return;
	}
	const ESupercutSymbol Symbol = Order[Plate];
	if (Symbol == Code[Progress])
	{
		Lit[Plate] = true;
		++Progress;
		if (Progress == Code.Num())
		{
			bSolved = true;
			FlashLeft = 0.f;   // a solved stand is all green, even straight after a wrong plate
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s completes the code"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
			PuzzleDoor(this, DoorId).SetOpen(true);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s counts, %d of %d"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol), Progress, Code.Num());
		}
	}
	else
	{
		Progress = 0;
		Lit.Init(false, Order.Num());
		FlashLeft = FSupercutTuning::Get().PlateFlashSeconds;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s is wrong, the code starts again"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
	}
	ShowState();
}

# Default: the uncooked project through the editor exe. With -Packaged: the packaged game.

#        [-Room <name>] [-Run <name>] [-Seed <n>] [-Log <file>] [-TimeoutSeconds 240] [-NoQuit] [-Packaged [-Exe <packaged Supercut.exe>]]
# Exit code: 0 the script finished, 2 the script failed (the player died when the script did not expect it,
# or a "scene" step did not see its room), 3 the game was stopped at the timeout.
param(

    [string]$Log = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\Logs\demo.log",
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 240,

# Makes the project's only content assets: one empty map and two materials.
# The game builds everything else in C++ at run time.
#
# Run headless from the project folder:
#   D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Supercut.uproject
#     -run=pythonscript -Script=D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Tools\make_assets.py -nullrhi -unattended -nopause -nosplash
#
# Safe to run again: it replaces what it made.

import unreal

MEL = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
EAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary
TOOLS = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def fresh(name, folder, asset_class, factory):
    path = folder + "/" + name
    if EAL.does_asset_exist(path):
        if not EAL.delete_asset(path):
            raise RuntimeError("could not delete " + path)
    asset = TOOLS.create_asset(name, folder, asset_class, factory)
    if asset is None:
        raise RuntimeError("could not create " + path)
    return asset


def vector_param(material, name, default, y):
    node = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, -500, y)
    node.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    node.set_editor_property("default_value", unreal.LinearColor(default[0], default[1], default[2], 1.0))
    return node


def scalar_param(material, name, default, y):
    node = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, -500, y)
    node.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    node.set_editor_property("default_value", default)
    return node


def make_solid():
    # A lit surface: Color, Rough, and Glow (an added self-lit colour, black by default).
    material = fresh("M_Solid", "/Game/Materials", unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    color = vector_param(material, "Color", (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 0)
    rough = scalar_param(material, "Rough", 0.8, 200)
    glow = vector_param(material, "Glow", (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 400)
    if not MEL.connect_material_property(color, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR):
        raise RuntimeError("M_Solid: base colour not connected")
    if not MEL.connect_material_property(rough, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS):
        raise RuntimeError("M_Solid: roughness not connected")
    if not MEL.connect_material_property(glow, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR):
        raise RuntimeError("M_Solid: emissive not connected")
    MEL.recompile_material(material)

void UAudioMixerBlueprintLibrary::StartRecordingOutput(const UObject* WorldContextObject, float ExpectedDuration, USoundSubmix* SubmixToRecord)
{
	if (Audio::FMixerDevice* MixerDevice = FAudioDeviceManager::GetAudioMixerDeviceFromWorldContext(WorldContextObject))
	{
		MixerDevice->StartRecording(SubmixToRecord, ExpectedDuration);
	}
	else
	{
		UE_LOGF(LogAudioMixer, Error, "Output recording is an audio mixer only feature.");
	}
}

USoundWave* UAudioMixerBlueprintLibrary::StopRecordingOutput(const UObject* WorldContextObject, EAudioRecordingExportType ExportType, const FString& Name, FString Path, USoundSubmix* SubmixToRecord, USoundWave* ExistingSoundWaveToOverwrite)
{
	// Name and Path come from Blueprint, so the file has to stay in the bounce folder.
	if (ExportType == EAudioRecordingExportType::WavFile && !Audio::CanWriteBouncedWavFile(Name, Path))
	{
		if (Audio::FMixerDevice* MixerDevice = FAudioDeviceManager::GetAudioMixerDeviceFromWorldContext(WorldContextObject))
		{
			float SampleRate = 0.0f;
			float ChannelCount = 0.0f;
			MixerDevice->StopRecording(SubmixToRecord, ChannelCount, SampleRate);
		}
		return nullptr;
	}

	return StopRecordingOutputToAnyPath(WorldContextObject, ExportType, Name, Path, SubmixToRecord, ExistingSoundWaveToOverwrite);
}

	// The default module's render mode comes from the command line. Both flags select the non-realtime renderer.
	Audio::EDeviceRenderMode GetDefaultRenderModeFromCommandLine()
	{
		if (FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("DeterministicAudio")))
		{
			return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::Deterministic;
		}
		if (FParse::Param(FCommandLine::Get(), TEXT("NonRealtimeAudio")))
		{
			return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::NonRealtime;
		}
		return Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::Realtime;
	}

	// Unset if no particular mode was requested; Realtime counts as no request, since it can't force a realtime device.
	TOptional<Audio::EDeviceRenderMode> GetRequestedRenderMode(const FAudioDeviceParams& InParams)
	{
		if (InParams.RenderMode.IsSet() && InParams.RenderMode.GetValue() != Audio::EDeviceRenderMode::Realtime)
		{
			return InParams.RenderMode;
		}
		return {};
	}

	FMixerPlatformNonRealtime::FMixerPlatformNonRealtime(float InSampleRate /*= 48000*/, float InNumChannels /*= 2*/)
		: SampleRate(InSampleRate)
		, NumChannels(InNumChannels)
		, TotalDurationRendered(0.0)
		, TotalDesiredRender(0.0)
		, TickDelta(0.0)
		, bIsInitialized(false)
		, bIsDeviceOpen(false)
	{
		ensureMsgf(InNumChannels == 2, TEXT("InNumChannels beyond stereo not exposed/tested and should be controlled via UI before removing this ensure."));
	}

	FMixerPlatformNonRealtime::~FMixerPlatformNonRealtime()
	{
	}

	void FMixerPlatformNonRealtime::RenderAudio(double NumSecondsToRender)
	{
		if (!bIsInitialized || !bIsDeviceOpen)
		{
			return;
		}

		const double TimePerCallback = ((double) AudioStreamInfo.NumOutputFrames) / AudioStreamInfo.DeviceInfo.SampleRate;

		// Increment how much audio time the user wants to have been rendered. 
		TotalDesiredRender += NumSecondsToRender;

		// Keep rendering audio until we surpass their desired time, TimePerCallback may be much smaller than NumSecondsToRender.
		while (TotalDurationRendered < TotalDesiredRender)
		{
			OutputBuffer.MixNextBuffer();

			ReadNextBuffer();
			TotalDurationRendered += TimePerCallback;
		}
	}

	void FMixerPlatformNonRealtime::OpenFileToWriteAudioTo(const FString& OutPath)
	{
		// Construct full path:
		FString AbsoluteFilePath;

		const bool bIsRelativePath = FPaths::IsRelative(OutPath);
		if (bIsRelativePath)
		{
			AbsoluteFilePath = FPaths::ProjectSavedDir() + OutPath;
			AbsoluteFilePath = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(AbsoluteFilePath);
		}
		else
		{
			AbsoluteFilePath = OutPath;
		}

		FSoundQualityInfo QualityInfo;
		QualityInfo.SampleRate = SampleRate;
		QualityInfo.NumChannels = NumChannels;
		QualityInfo.Quality = 100;

		// Gotcha for bouncing wav files: this has to be filled in.
		QualityInfo.Duration = 5.0f;
		QualityInfo.SampleDataSize = 5.0f * SampleRate * NumChannels * sizeof(int16);

		AudioFileWriter.Reset(new FAudioFileWriter(AbsoluteFilePath, QualityInfo));
	}

FVector UCharacterMovementComponent::GetFallingLateralAcceleration(float DeltaTime)
{
	// No acceleration in Z
	FVector FallAcceleration = ProjectToGravityFloor(Acceleration);

	// bound acceleration, falling object has minimal ability to impact acceleration
	if (!HasAnimRootMotion() && FallAcceleration.SizeSquared() > 0.f)
	{
		FallAcceleration = GetAirControl(DeltaTime, AirControl, FallAcceleration);
		FallAcceleration = FallAcceleration.GetClampedToMaxSize(GetMaxAcceleration());
	}

	return FallAcceleration;
}


bool UCharacterMovementComponent::ShouldLimitAirControl(float DeltaTime, const FVector& FallAcceleration) const
{
	return (ProjectToGravityFloor(FallAcceleration).SizeSquared() > 0.f);
}

FVector UCharacterMovementComponent::GetAirControl(float DeltaTime, float TickAirControl, const FVector& FallAcceleration)
{
	// Boost
	if (TickAirControl != 0.f)
	{
		TickAirControl = BoostAirControl(DeltaTime, TickAirControl, FallAcceleration);
	}

	return TickAirControl * FallAcceleration;
}

void UCharacterMovementComponent::SetGravityDirection(const FVector& InNewGravityDir)
{
	FVector NewGravityDir = InNewGravityDir.GetSafeNormal();
	if (ensure(!NewGravityDir.IsNearlyZero()))
	{
		if (!GravityDirection.Equals(NewGravityDir))
		{

```
bool FParse::Value(
	const TCHAR*	Stream,
	const TCHAR*	Match,
	TCHAR*			Value,
	int32			MaxLen,
	bool			bShouldStopOnSeparator,
	const TCHAR**	OptStreamGotTo
)
{
	if (MaxLen == 0)
	{
		return false;
	}
	check(Value && MaxLen > 0);

	bool bSuccess = false;
	int32 MatchLen = FCString::Strlen(Match);

	if (OptStreamGotTo)
	{
		*OptStreamGotTo = nullptr;
	}

	const TCHAR* FoundInStream = FCString::Strifind(Stream, Match, true);
	if (FoundInStream == nullptr)
	{
		Value[0] = TCHAR('\0');
		return false;
	}

	const TCHAR* ValueStartInStream = FoundInStream + MatchLen;
	const TCHAR* ValueEndInStream;

	// Check for quoted arguments' string with spaces
	// -Option="Value1 Value2"
	//         ^~~~Start
	const bool bArgumentsQuoted = *ValueStartInStream == '"';

	if (bArgumentsQuoted)
	{
		// Skip quote character if only params were quoted.
		ValueStartInStream += 1;
		ValueEndInStream = FCString::Strstr(ValueStartInStream, TEXT("\x22"));

		if (ValueEndInStream == nullptr)
		{
			// this should probably log a warning if bArgumentsQuoted is true, as we started with a '"' and didn't find the terminating one.
			ValueEndInStream = FoundInStream + FCString::Strlen(FoundInStream);
		}
	}
	else
	{
		// Skip initial whitespace
		const TCHAR* WhiteSpaceChars = TEXT(" \r\n\t");
		ValueStartInStream += FCString::Strspn(ValueStartInStream, WhiteSpaceChars);

		// Non-quoted string without spaces.
		const TCHAR* TerminatingChars = bShouldStopOnSeparator ? TEXT(",) \r\n\t") : WhiteSpaceChars;
		ValueEndInStream = ValueStartInStream + FCString::Strcspn(ValueStartInStream, TerminatingChars);
	}

	int32 ValueLength = FMath::Min<int32>(MaxLen - 1, UE_PTRDIFF_TO_INT32(ValueEndInStream - ValueStartInStream));
	// It is possible for ValueLength to be 0.
	// FCString::Strncpy asserts that its copying at least 1 char, memcpy has no such constraint.
	FMemory::Memcpy(Value, ValueStartInStream, sizeof(Value[0]) * ValueLength);
	Value[ValueLength] = TCHAR('\0');

	if (OptStreamGotTo)
	{
		if (bArgumentsQuoted && *ValueEndInStream == '"')
		{
			++ValueEndInStream;
		}

		*OptStreamGotTo = ValueEndInStream;
	}

	return true;
}

}

/**
 * The command-line invocation string, processed using the standard Windows CommandLineToArgvW implementation.
 * This need to be a static global to avoid object unwinding errors in WinMain when SEH is enabled.
 */
static FString GSavedCommandLine;

AUTORTFM_DISABLE bool ProcessCommandLine()
{
	int argc = 0;
	LPWSTR* argv = ::CommandLineToArgvW(::GetCommandLineW(), &argc);
	if (argv != nullptr)
	{
		// Reconstruct our command line string in a format suitable for consumption by the FParse class
		GSavedCommandLine = "";
		for (int32 Option = 1; Option < argc; Option++)
		{
			GSavedCommandLine += TEXT(" ");
			
			// Inject quotes in the correct position to preserve arguments containing whitespace
			FString Temp = argv[Option];
			if (Temp.Contains(TEXT(" ")))
			{
				int32 Quote = 0;
				if(Temp.StartsWith(TEXT("-")))
				{
					int32 Separator;
					if (Temp.FindChar('=', Separator))
					{
						Quote = Separator + 1;
					}
				}
				Temp = Temp.Left(Quote) + TEXT("\"") + Temp.Mid(Quote) + TEXT("\"");
			}
			GSavedCommandLine += Temp;
		}
		
		// Free memory allocated for CommandLineToArgvW() arguments
		::LocalFree(argv);
		return true;
	}
	
	return false;
}

AUTORTFM_DISABLE LAUNCH_API int32 LaunchWindowsStartup( HINSTANCE hInInstance, HINSTANCE hPrevInstance, char*, int32 nCmdShow, const TCHAR* CmdLine )
{
	TRACE_BOOKMARK(TEXT("WinMain.Enter"));
#if USING_ADDRESS_SANITISER
	__asan_set_error_report_callback(ASanErrorCallback);
#endif

	// Setup common Windows settings
	SetupWindowsEnvironment();

	int32 ErrorLevel			= 0;
	hInstance				= hInInstance;

	if (!CmdLine)
	{
		CmdLine = ::GetCommandLineW();

		// Attempt to process the command-line arguments using the standard Windows implementation
		// (This ensures behavior parity with other platforms where argc and argv are used.)
		if ( ProcessCommandLine() )
		{
			CmdLine = *GSavedCommandLine;
		}
	}

	// If we're running in unattended mode, make sure we never display error dialogs if we crash.
	if ( FParse::Param( CmdLine, TEXT("unattended") ) )
	{
		SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX | SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX);
	}

struct FSupercutTuning
{
	// ---- Player movement ----
	float WalkSpeed = 600.f;             // Top ground speed, cm/s.
	float JumpApex = 110.f;              // Height of a standing jump, cm.
	float GravityScale = 2.0f;           // Multiplies gravity for the player. The apex stays the same; higher makes the jump shorter and snappier.
	float AirControl = 0.5f;             // 0 to 1. How much the player can steer in the air.
	float CoyoteTime = 0.1f;             // A jump still works this long after walking off an edge.

void ASupercutCharacter::OnJumped_Implementation()

void ASupercutCharacter::Landed(const FHitResult& Hit)
{
	Super::Landed(Hit);
	const float FallSpeed = FMath::Abs(GetCharacterMovement()->Velocity.Z);
	CameraDip = FMath::Clamp(FallSpeed / 1300.f, 0.f, 1.f) * FSupercutTuning::Get().LandingDip;
	if (bTrackingJump)
	{
		bTrackingJump = false;
		LastJumpApex = JumpPeakZ - JumpStartZ;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("JUMP apex %.1f cm"), LastJumpApex);
	}
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::RunStep(const FStep& Step, FSupercutInput& Input, ASupercutCharacter* Hero)
{
	auto Number = [&Step](int32 Index)
	{
		if (!Step.Args.IsValidIndex(Index))
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("SCRIPT: \"%s\" at %.2f needs %d numbers"), *Step.Command, Step.Time, Index + 1);
		}
		return FCString::Atof(*Step.Args[Index]);
	};

	const FVector At = Hero->GetActorLocation();
	FString Note;

	if (Step.Command == TEXT("move"))
	{
		HeldForward = Number(0);
		HeldRight = Number(1);
	}
	else if (Step.Command == TEXT("look"))
	{
		SetControlRotation(FRotator(Number(1), Number(0), 0.f));
	}
	else if (Step.Command == TEXT("lookat"))
	{
		LookAt(FVector(Number(0), Number(1), Number(2)), Hero);
	}
	else if (Step.Command == TEXT("aim"))
	{
		const int32 EnemyIndex = FMath::RoundToInt(Number(0));
		ASupercutEnemy* Enemy = nullptr;
		for (TActorIterator<ASupercutEnemy> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)
		{
			if (It->GetIndex() == EnemyIndex && !It->IsDying())
			{
				Enemy = *It;
			}
		}
		if (Enemy)
		{
			LookAt(Enemy->GetChestLocation(), Hero);
			Note = FString::Printf(TEXT(" %s at %s, health %d"), *FString(Enemy->GetKindName()).ToLower(), *Enemy->GetActorLocation().ToCompactString(), Enemy->GetHealth());
		}
		else
		{
			Note = TEXT(" enemy is gone, view unchanged");
		}
	}
	else if (Step.Command == TEXT("jump"))
	{
	Input.Right = (IsInputKeyDown(EKeys::D) ? 1.f : 0.f) - (IsInputKeyDown(EKeys::A) ? 1.f : 0.f);

	float MouseX = 0.f;
	float MouseY = 0.f;
	GetInputMouseDelta(MouseX, MouseY);
	const float Speed = FSupercutTuning::Get().LookDegreesPerMouseUnit;
	Input.YawDegrees = MouseX * Speed;
	Input.PitchDegrees = MouseY * Speed;   // the engine's mouse Y is already positive for "up"

	Input.bJump = WasInputKeyJustPressed(EKeys::SpaceBar);

void ASupercutRusher::TickLunge(float DeltaSeconds, AActor* TargetActor)
{
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const FVector Here = GetActorLocation();
	FVector Next = Here + LungeDirection * FMath::Min(Tuning.RusherLungeSpeed * DeltaSeconds, LungeLeft);
	const FVector2D Clamped = ClampToHome(Next);
	const bool bAtHomeEdge = !FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Clamped.X, Next.X) || !FMath::IsNearlyEqual(Clamped.Y, Next.Y);
	Next.X = Clamped.X;
	Next.Y = Clamped.Y;
	FHitResult Hit;
	SetActorLocation(Next, true, &Hit);
	LungeLeft -= FVector::Dist2D(Here, GetActorLocation());

	// The first touch ends the lunge, so a lunge hurts once.
	if (Touches(TargetActor))
	{
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUSHER %d lunge hits the player for %.0f"), GetIndex(), Tuning.RusherLungeDamage);
		CastChecked<ASupercutCharacter>(TargetActor)->TakeHit(Tuning.RusherLungeDamage, LungeDirection);
		EndLunge(TEXT("it hit the player"));
	}
	else if (Hit.bBlockingHit)
	{
		EndLunge(FString::Printf(TEXT("stopped by %s"), Hit.GetActor() ? *Hit.GetActor()->GetName() : TEXT("the floor")));
	}
	else if (bAtHomeEdge)
	{
		EndLunge(TEXT("stopped at the edge of its home area"));
	}
	else if (LungeLeft <= KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER)
	{
		EndLunge(TEXT("missed"));
	}
}

void ASupercutRusher::EndLunge(const FString& How)
{
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUSHER %d lunge ends: %s, %.0f cm short of its full length"), GetIndex(), *How, FMath::Max(0.f, LungeLeft));
	Enter(ERusherState::Recover);
}

{

};

	World.Run(0.4f);
	TestEqual(TEXT("a moving shot does hurt"), Player->GetHealth(), Tuning.PlayerHealth - Tuning.GruntShotDamage);
	return true;
}

import os
def edit(p, pairs):
    b=open(p,'rb').read().decode('utf-8')
    crlf='\r\n' in b
    s=b.replace('\r\n','\n')
    for old,new in pairs:

185	## 4. Notes for the helper wiring it into the game
186	
187	**Start the four action stems in sync.** They are the same length to the sample (1,280,000) and must start on the
188	same sample. The cleanest way I know of is one MetaSound with four Wave Player nodes (looping on), all started by the
189	same trigger, with one gain input per stem (one source, one clock). `[docs, not verified on 5.9 here]`. Check the
190	node names against the 5.9 editor. Four separate audio components started on the same frame may drift by a buffer.
191	Use one shared start time if you go that way.
192	
193	**Import settings.** The loops are exact only if the engine plays them exact. Some compressed formats pad or
194	re-encode the loop point. Test a stem looping in game; if you hear a bump at 26.67 s, set the music to uncompressed
195	PCM or the engine's loop-safe setting.
196	
197	**Bar lines in samples.** Bar k (counting from 0) starts at k x 80,000. Beat = 20,000 samples = 0.41667 s. A 16-bar
198	loop is 1,280,000 samples; `mx_between` is 640,000. The stingers' downbeat: `mx_take_start` at 0.3325 s
199	(15,960 samples), `mx_room_clear` at 0.4367 s (20,960 samples).
200	
201	**Fades.** A loop's first sample is not zero (that is what makes the end join the start). Start a loop with a 5 to
202	10 ms fade-in and stop it with a 5 to 10 ms fade-out, or the start and stop will click.
203	
204	**The cut (CUT!).** Stop all music stems dead on the snap frame, with a 5 ms fade so it does not click. Let the
205	frozen bed take over as the sound lane describes. The room tail is cut too: that is the joke, the take stops.
206	
207	**Bringing it back (ACTION!).** Two options, both cheap to test:
208	
209	1. Resume from the sample where it stopped (the brief's suggestion). It works, since no melody runs long, but the
210	   music comes back mid-note and mid-bar, often on a weak 16th, and needs a short fade-in.
211	2. My pick: resume from the start of the bar it was cut in, position = floor(position / 80,000) x 80,000. Every bar
212	   opens with the low drum, the bass root and a chord, so the score comes back on a downbeat that lines up with
213	   `sc_freeze_out`'s hit, like a fresh take of the same bar. It repeats at most 1.67 s of music. To keep the hit and
214	   the downbeat together, start the stems on the frame the world resumes (the sound lane times `freeze_out`'s hit to
215	   that frame).
216	
217	Do not restart from bar 1: the run would hear its first two bars over and over.

void UMovieGraphDefaultAudioRenderer::ProcessAudioTick()
{
	// Only supported on the new audio mixer (with the non-realtime device, windows only).
	Audio::FMixerDevice* MixerDevice = UE::MovieGraph::Audio::GetAudioMixerDeviceFromWorldContext(this);
	if (!MixerDevice)
	{
		return;
	}

	const Audio::IAudioMixerPlatformInterface* AudioMixerPlatform = MixerDevice->GetAudioMixerPlatform();
	Audio::FMixerPlatformNonRealtime* NRTPlatform = nullptr;
	if (AudioMixerPlatform && AudioMixerPlatform->IsNonRealtime())
	{
		// There is only one non-realtime audio platform at this time, so we can safely static_cast this due to the IsNonRealtime check.
		NRTPlatform = static_cast<Audio::FMixerPlatformNonRealtime*>(MixerDevice->GetAudioMixerPlatform());
	}

	if (!NRTPlatform)
	{
		return;
	}

	const TArray<TObjectPtr<UMoviePipelineExecutorShot>>& ActiveShotList = GetOwningGraph()->GetActiveShotList();
	const int32 CurrentShotIndex = GetOwningGraph()->GetCurrentShotIndex();
	const TObjectPtr<UMoviePipelineExecutorShot> CurrentShot = ActiveShotList[CurrentShotIndex];

	if (CurrentShot->ShotInfo.State == EMovieRenderShotState::WarmingUp)
	{
		SetMovieSceneAudioRecording(GetOwningGraph(), true);
	}

	// Start capturing any produced samples on the same frame we start submitting samples that will make it to disk.
	// This comes before we process samples for this frame (below).

		StartAudioRecording();
	}

# Makes the project's only content assets: one empty map and two materials.
# The game builds everything else in C++ at run time.
#
# Run headless from the project folder:
#   D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59\Supercut.uproject

#
# Safe to run again: it replaces what it made.

import unreal

MEL = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
EAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary
TOOLS = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def fresh(name, folder, asset_class, factory):
    path = folder + "/" + name
    if EAL.does_asset_exist(path):
        if not EAL.delete_asset(path):
            raise RuntimeError("could not delete " + path)
    asset = TOOLS.create_asset(name, folder, asset_class, factory)
    if asset is None:
        raise RuntimeError("could not create " + path)
    return asset


def vector_param(material, name, default, y):
    node = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, -500, y)
    node.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    node.set_editor_property("default_value", unreal.LinearColor(default[0], default[1], default[2], 1.0))
    return node


def scalar_param(material, name, default, y):
    node = MEL.create_material_expression(material, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, -500, y)
    node.set_editor_property("parameter_name", name)
    node.set_editor_property("default_value", default)
    return node


def make_solid():
    # A lit surface: Color, Rough, and Glow (an added self-lit colour, black by default).
    material = fresh("M_Solid", "/Game/Materials", unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    color = vector_param(material, "Color", (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), 0)
    rough = scalar_param(material, "Rough", 0.8, 200)
    glow = vector_param(material, "Glow", (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 400)

    if not MEL.connect_material_property(glow, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR):

void ASupercutPlayerController::LoadScript(const FString& Path)
{
	TArray<FString> Lines;
	if (!FFileHelper::LoadFileToStringArray(Lines, *Path))
	{
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("-SupercutScript: cannot read %s"), *Path);
	}
	for (const FString& Raw : Lines)
	{
		const FString Line = Raw.TrimStartAndEnd();
		if (Line.IsEmpty() || Line.StartsWith(TEXT("#")))
		{
			continue;
		}
		TArray<FString> Words;
		Line.ParseIntoArrayWS(Words);
		if (Words.Num() < 2)
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Fatal, TEXT("-SupercutScript: bad line \"%s\" in %s"), *Line, *Path);
		}
		FStep Step;
		Step.Time = FCString::Atof(*Words[0]);
		Step.Command = Words[1].ToLower();
		for (int32 Index = 2; Index < Words.Num(); ++Index)
		{
			Step.Args.Add(Words[Index]);
		}
		Steps.Add(Step);
	}
	bScripted = true;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SCRIPT loaded: %d steps from %s"), Steps.Num(), *Path);
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::PlayerTick(float DeltaTime)
{
	Super::PlayerTick(DeltaTime);

	if (WasInputKeyJustPressed(EKeys::Escape))
	{
		Quit(0);
		return;
	}

	// A key a script pressed last frame has been seen by the engine now. Let it go.
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- The scripted player

void ASupercutPlayerController::FailScript(const FString& Why)
{
	bScriptOver = true;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Error, TEXT("SCRIPT failed at %.2f s: %s"), ScriptClock, *Why);
	ReportFps();
	if (bQuitAtEnd)
	{
		Quit(2);
	}
}

```
void ASupercutGlyph::BeginPlay()
{
	Super::BeginPlay();
	const FSupercutTuning& Tuning = FSupercutTuning::Get();
	const float Size = Tuning.GlyphSize;
	UMaterialInterface* Ink = SupercutShapes::Glow(this, PuzzleCyan, Tuning.PuzzleGlow);
	PuzzleAddSymbol(this, RootComponent, Symbol, FVector(1.f, 0.f, 0.f), Size, Ink);
	// One pip per place in the code, in a row under the symbol.
	for (int32 Pip = 0; Pip < Order; ++Pip)
	{
		const float Side = (0.5f * (Order - 1) - Pip) * Size * 0.28f;
		UStaticMeshComponent* Part = SupercutShapes::Add(this, RootComponent, ESupercutShape::Cube, FVector(1.f, Side, -Size * 0.75f), FRotator::ZeroRotator, FVector(2.f, Size * 0.14f, Size * 0.14f), Ink);
		Part->SetCastShadow(false);
	}

	USupercutTime& Time = USupercutTime::Get(this);
	Time.OnFroze.AddWeakLambda(this, [this]() { ShowFor(true); });
	Time.OnResumed.AddWeakLambda(this, [this]() { ShowFor(false); });
	ShowFor(Time.IsFrozen());
}

void ASupercutGlyph::ShowFor(bool bFrozen)
{
	SetActorHiddenInGame(!bFrozen);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Switch

ASupercutSwitch::ASupercutSwitch()
{
	PrimaryActorTick.bCanEverTick = true;
	RootComponent = CreateDefaultSubobject<USceneComponent>(TEXT("Root"));
}

void ASupercutSwitch::Setup(const FString& InDoorId, float InSeconds)
{
	DoorId = InDoorId;
	Seconds = InSeconds;
	USupercutTime::Get(this).JoinScene(this);
	ShowState();
}

void ASupercutDoor::SetOpen(bool bInOpen)
{
	if (bInOpen == bOpen)
	{
		return;
	}
	bOpen = bInOpen;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("DOOR %s %s"), *Id, bOpen ? TEXT("opens") : TEXT("shuts"));
	ShowState();
}

void ASupercutDoor::ShowState()
	if (Symbol == Code[Progress])
	{
		Lit[Plate] = true;
		++Progress;
		if (Progress == Code.Num())
		{
			bSolved = true;
			FlashLeft = 0.f;   // a solved stand is all green, even straight after a wrong plate
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s completes the code"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
			PuzzleDoor(this, DoorId).SetOpen(true);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s counts, %d of %d"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol), Progress, Code.Num());
		}
	}
	else
	{
		Progress = 0;
		Lit.Init(false, Order.Num());
		FlashLeft = FSupercutTuning::Get().PlateFlashSeconds;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s is wrong, the code starts again"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
	}
	ShowState();
}

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "SupercutEnemy.h"
#include "SupercutRusher.generated.h"

class UMaterialInstanceDynamic;

/** What a Rusher is doing. */
enum class ERusherState : uint8
{
	Run,      // runs straight at the player while it can see them
	Windup,   // stopped, crouches, its visor glows: the warning
	Lunge,    // a straight dash along the direction fixed at the end of the windup
	Recover,  // stands still after a lunge
};

/**
 * The second enemy kind: it makes the player move or freeze.
 *
 * Low, wide and leaning forward, with two horns and no gun, and a cyan visor. It runs at the player,
 * stops close by and crouches for a moment, then lunges in a straight line. A lunge that touches the
 * player hurts them once. A sidestep while it crouches makes the lunge miss, because the direction
 * is fixed when the crouch ends. After a lunge it stands still, open to shots.
 *
 * Like the Grunt it moves by sweeping its capsule along the floor inside a home area.
 */
UCLASS()
class ASupercutRusher : public ASupercutEnemy
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutRusher();

	/** Call before BeginPlay. Home is the floor area it may run and lunge in. */
	void Setup(int32 InIndex, const FBox2D& InHome);

	virtual const TCHAR* GetKindName() const override { return TEXT("RUSHER"); }

	ERusherState GetState() const { return State; }
	/** The lunge's direction along the floor. Fixed at the end of the windup. */
	FVector GetLungeDirection() const { return LungeDirection; }

protected:
	virtual int32 GetStartHealth() const override;
	virtual void BuildBody() override;
	virtual void TickCombat(float DeltaSeconds, AActor* TargetActor) override;

private:
	void Enter(ERusherState NewState);
	void TickLunge(float DeltaSeconds, AActor* TargetActor);
	void EndLunge(const FString& How, float Rest);
	bool Touches(const AActor* TargetActor) const;
	void UpdatePose();

	UPROPERTY()
	TObjectPtr<UMaterialInstanceDynamic> VisorMaterial;

	ERusherState State = ERusherState::Run;
	float StateClock = 0.f;
	FVector LungeDirection = FVector::ForwardVector;
	float LungeLeft = 0.f;
	float RestFor = 0.f;   // how long this Recover lasts
};

		return A;
	}
	// A triangle wave: out at a steady speed, back at the same speed.
	const float Along = FMath::Fmod(AtClock * Speed, 2.f * Length);
	const float Alpha = (Along <= Length ? Along : 2.f * Length - Along) / Length;
	return FMath::Lerp(A, B, Alpha);
}

{

	}
	Clock += DeltaSeconds;
	SetActorLocation(LocationAt(Clock));
}

void ASupercutDoor::SetOpen(bool bInOpen)
{
	if (bInOpen == bOpen)
	{
		return;
	}
	bOpen = bInOpen;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("DOOR %s %s"), *Id, bOpen ? TEXT("opens") : TEXT("shuts"));
	ShowState();
}

void ASupercutPlates::HitPlate(int32 Plate)
{
	if (bSolved)
	{
		return;
	}
	const ESupercutSymbol Symbol = Order[Plate];
	if (Symbol == Code[Progress])
	{
		Lit[Plate] = true;
		++Progress;
		if (Progress == Code.Num())
		{
			bSolved = true;
			FlashLeft = 0.f;   // a solved stand is all green, even straight after a wrong plate
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s completes the code"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
			PuzzleDoor(this, DoorId).SetOpen(true);
		}
		else
		{
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s counts, %d of %d"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol), Progress, Code.Num());
		}
	}
	else
	{
		Progress = 0;
		Lit.Init(false, Order.Num());
		FlashLeft = FSupercutTuning::Get().PlateFlashSeconds;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PLATES door %s: %s is wrong, the code starts again"), *DoorId, PuzzleSymbolName(Symbol));
	}
	ShowState();
}

void ASupercutSwitch::TakeShot()
{
	TimeLeft = Seconds;
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SWITCH door %s: hit, the door is open for %.1f s of scene time"), *DoorId, Seconds);
	PuzzleDoor(this, DoorId).SetOpen(true);
	ShowState();
}

void ASupercutSwitch::Tick(float DeltaSeconds)
{
	Super::Tick(DeltaSeconds);
	if (TimeLeft <= 0.f)
	{
		return;
	}
	// Scene time: a freeze stops the clock.
	const int32 LitBefore = GetLitSegments();
	TimeLeft -= DeltaSeconds;
	if (TimeLeft <= 0.f)
	{
		TimeLeft = 0.f;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("SWITCH door %s: time is up"), *DoorId);
		PuzzleDoor(this, DoorId).SetOpen(false);
	}
	if (GetLitSegments() != LitBefore)
	{
		ShowState();
	}
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::PlayerTick(float DeltaTime)
{
	Super::PlayerTick(DeltaTime);

	if (WasInputKeyJustPressed(EKeys::Escape))
	{
		Quit(0);
		return;
	}

	// A key a script pressed last frame has been seen by the engine now. Let it go.
	for (const FKey& Key : KeysToLetGo)
	{
		PressKey(Key, false);
	}
	KeysToLetGo.Reset();
	ScriptClick.Reset();

	USupercutRun& Run = USupercutRun::Get(this);
	ASupercutCharacter* Hero = Cast<ASupercutCharacter>(GetPawn());
	if (!Hero)
	{
		return;
	}

	FSupercutInput Input;
	if (bScripted)
	{
		RunScript(DeltaTime, Input, Hero, Run);
	}
	else
	{
		ReadKeys(Input);
		FInputModeGameAndUI Mode;
		Mode.SetHideCursorDuringCapture(false);
		SetInputMode(Mode);
	}
	else
	{
		SetInputMode(FInputModeGameOnly());
	}
}

int32 ASupercutPlayerController::CardAt(const FVector2D& Pixel) const
{
	int32 Width = 0;
	int32 Height = 0;
	GetViewportSize(Width, Height);
	const int32 Count = USupercutRun::Get(this).GetOffer().Num();
	for (int32 Card = 0; Card < Count; ++Card)
	{
		if (ASupercutHUD::CardRect(Card, Count, Width, Height).IsInside(Pixel))
		{
			return Card;
		}
	}
	return INDEX_NONE;
}

void ASupercutPlayerController::TickPick(USupercutRun& Run)
{
	if (Run.GetSecondsInPhase() < FSupercutTuning::Get().PickKeyDelay)
	{
		return;
	}

	int32 Card = INDEX_NONE;
	const FKey NumberKeys[] = { EKeys::One, EKeys::Two, EKeys::Three };
	for (int32 Index = 0; Index < UE_ARRAY_COUNT(NumberKeys); ++Index)
	{
		if (WasInputKeyJustPressed(NumberKeys[Index]))
		{
			Card = Index;
		}
	}

	bool bByMouse = false;
	if (Card == INDEX_NONE)
	{
		TOptional<FVector2D> Click = ScriptClick;
		double MouseX = 0.0;
		double MouseY = 0.0;
		if (!bScripted && WasInputKeyJustPressed(EKeys::LeftMouseButton) && GetMousePosition(MouseX, MouseY))
		{
			Click = FVector2D(MouseX, MouseY);
		}
		if (Click.IsSet())
		{
			Card = CardAt(Click.GetValue());
			bByMouse = Card != INDEX_NONE;
			UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK click at %.0f,%.0f: %s"), Click->X, Click->Y, bByMouse ? *FString::Printf(TEXT("card %d"), Card + 1) : TEXT("no card there"));
		}
	}

	if (Card != INDEX_NONE && Run.Pick(Card))
	{
		bFireLocked = bByMouse;
	}
}

imported: the game reads Audio/music/wav itself (SupercutMusic.cpp).\n#\n# Run headless from the project folder:\n#   D:\\UE\\UE_5.9\\Engine\\Binaries\\Win64\\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe one line per sound (name, looping, compression, loading, channels, length), so two runs\n# can be compared line by line.\n\nimport json\nimport os\n\nimport unreal\n\nEAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary\nTOOLS = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()\nFOLDER = \"/Game/Audio\"\nSOURCE = os.path.join(unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir()), \"Audio\", \"wav\")\n\n\ndef import_wave(file_name, looping):\n    name = os.path.splitext(file_name)[0]\n    path = FOLDER + \"/\" + name\n    if EAL.does_asset_exist(path) and not EAL.delete_asset(path):\n        raise RuntimeError(\"could not delete \" + path)\n    source = os.path.join(SOURCE, file_name)\n    if not os.path.isfile(source):\n        raise RuntimeError(\"missing \" + source)\n\n    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()\n    task.set_editor_property(\"filename\", source)\n    task.set_editor_property(\"destination_path\", FOLDER)\n    task.set_editor_property(\"destination_name\", name)\n    task.set_editor_property(\"automated\", True)\n    task.set_editor_property(\"replace_existing\", True)\n    task.set_editor_property(\"save\", False)\n    TOOLS.import_asset_tasks([task])\n\n    wave = unreal.load_asset(path)\n    if not isinstance(wave, unreal.SoundWave):\n        raise RuntimeError(\"import of \" + source + \" gave \" + str(wave))\n    wave.set_sound_asset_compression_type(unreal.SoundAssetCompressionType.PCM)\n    wave.set_editor_property(\"looping\", looping)\n return wave\n\n\ndef main():\n    with open(os.path.join(SOURCE, \"manifest.json\"), encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        manifest = json.load(handle)\n    lines = []\n    for sound in manifest:\n wave.get_editor_property(\"loading_behavior\"), wave.get_editor_property(\"num_channels\"), wave.get_editor_property(\"duration\")))\n    for line in lines:\n        unreal.log(line)\n    unreal.log(\"SOUND ASSETS made: %d\" % len(lines))\n\n\nmain()\n"

# Builds one target of this project and survives the bad precompiled header trap.
# Usage: powershell -File Tools\build.ps1 [-Target SupercutEditor|Supercut] [-Engine D:\UE\UE_5.9] [-Jobs 1]
#
# The trap: on this PC the compiler sometimes writes a 2 GB+ shared precompiled header that is bad, with no
# error. Every file compiled against it then dies with "C1001 ... msc1.cpp, line 1589", and the build tool keeps
# reusing the bad header because it looks up to date. Seen on UE 5.8.4 and 5.9, with one job and with several.
# The only cure found is to delete the header and build it again. This script does that, up to 3 times, and
# says so each time. Any other failure is returned as it is.
param(
    [ValidateSet("SupercutEditor", "Supercut")] [string]$Target = "SupercutEditor",
    [string]$Engine = "D:\UE\UE_5.9",
    [int]$Jobs = 1
)
$proj = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$uproject = Join-Path $proj "Supercut.uproject"
$logDir = Join-Path $proj "Saved\Logs"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $logDir | Out-Null
$log = Join-Path $logDir "ubt_$Target.log"
$pchDir = Join-Path $proj "Intermediate\Build\Win64\x64\$Target\Development"

for ($try = 1; $try -le 4; $try++) {
    & "$Engine\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat" $Target Win64 Development "-project=$uproject" -waitmutex "-MaxParallelActions=$Jobs" "-Log=$log" | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($code -eq 0) { Write-Output "build $Target on ${Engine}: exit 0 (try $try)"; exit 0 }
    $badHeader = Select-String -Path $log -Pattern "msc1\.cpp', line 1589" -Quiet
    if (-not $badHeader -or $try -eq 4) {
        Select-String -Path $log -Pattern "error |Result:" | Select-Object -First 20 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
        Write-Output "build $Target on ${Engine}: exit $code (try $try). Log: $log"
        exit $code
    }

# Runs the headless automation tests and prints one line per test, then the exit code.
# Usage: powershell -File Tools\run_tests.ps1 [-Filter Supercut] [-Log <file>]
# Exit code: 0 every test passed, anything else a test failed or the editor did not finish.
param(
    [string]$Filter = "Supercut",
    [string]$Log = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\Logs\tests.log",
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 600
)
$exe = "D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe"
$testArgs = @(
    "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Supercut.uproject",
    "-ExecCmds=`"Automation RunTests $Filter; Quit`"",
    "-nullrhi", "-unattended", "-nopause", "-nosplash", "-stdout", "-FullStdOutLogOutput"
)
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $testArgs -PassThru -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput $Log
$null = $p.Handle   # without this PowerShell does not keep the exit code of a process it did not wait on
if (-not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)) {
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force
    Write-Output "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s: the test run was stopped"
    exit 3
}
Select-String -Path $Log -Pattern "Test Completed\. Result=|TEST COMPLETE|LogAutomationController: Error|LogSupercut: Error|Fatal error" |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Line -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[ 0-9]*\]', '' }
$passed = @(Select-String -Path $Log -Pattern "Test Completed\. Result=\{Success\}").Count
$failed = @(Select-String -Path $Log -Pattern "Test Completed\. Result=\{(?!Success)").Count
Write-Output "tests passed $passed, failed $failed, exit code $($p.ExitCode)"
exit $p.ExitCode

{
	const float TestStep = 0.01f;   // seconds per tick

	/** A game world with the plain engine game mode, so no room is built. */
	struct FSupercutTestWorld : FTestWorldWrapper
	{
		bool Start()
		{
			if (!CreateTestWorld(EWorldType::Game))
			{
				return false;
			}
			GetTestWorld()->GetWorldSettings()->DefaultGameMode = AGameModeBase::StaticClass();
			return BeginPlayInTestWorld();
		}

		void Run(float Seconds)
		{
			const int32 Ticks = FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / TestStep);
			for (int32 Tick = 0; Tick < Ticks; ++Tick)
			{
				TickTestWorld(TestStep);
			}
		}

		template <typename T>
		T* Spawn(const FVector& Location, const FRotator& Rotation = FRotator::ZeroRotator)
		{
			FActorSpawnParameters Params;
			Params.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;
			return GetTestWorld()->SpawnActor<T>(Location, Rotation, Params);
		}

		USupercutTime& Time() { return USupercutTime::Get(GetTestWorld()); }

		template <typename T>
		int32 Count()
		{
			int32 Found = 0;
			for (TActorIterator<T> It(GetTestWorld()); It; ++It)
			{
				++Found;
			}
			return Found;
		}
	};

	const EAutomationTestFlags SupercutTestFlags = EAutomationTestFlags_ApplicationContextMask | EAutomationTestFlags::ProductFilter;
}

	TestEqual(TEXT("charges at the start match the tuning"), Time.GetCharges(), Full);

	for (int32 Use = 1; Use <= Full; ++Use)
	{
		TestTrue(TEXT("a press with a charge left freezes"), Time.PressClapper());
		TestTrue(TEXT("frozen after the press"), Time.IsFrozen());
		TestEqual(TEXT("one charge spent"), Time.GetCharges(), Full - Use);
		World.Run(0.1f);

		TestEqual(TEXT("ending a freeze costs no charge"), Time.GetCharges(), Full - Use);
		World.Run(0.1f);
	}

# Usage: powershell -File Tools\run_demo.ps1 [-Shots <folder>] [-ResX 1280] [-ResY 720] [-Script <file>]
#        [-Room <name>] [-Run <name>] [-Seed <n>] [-Log <file>] [-TimeoutSeconds 240] [-NoQuit] [-Packaged [-Exe <packaged Supercut.exe>]]
# Exit code: 0 the script finished, 2 the script failed (the player died when the script did not expect it,
# or a "scene" step did not see its room), 3 the game was stopped at the timeout.
param(
    [string]$Shots = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\shots",
    [int]$ResX = 1280,
    [int]$ResY = 720,
    [string]$Script = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Script\demo.txt",
    [string]$Room = "",   # play one room, Content\Rooms\<name>.txt, as a run of its own
    [string]$Run = "",    # play the run list Content\Runs\<name>.txt instead of main.txt
    [int]$Seed = -1,      # the seed that decides which upgrades are offered; -1 leaves it to the game
    [string]$Log = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\Logs\demo.log",
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 240,
    [switch]$NoQuit,   # leave out -SupercutQuit: the game keeps running after the script and is stopped at the timeout
    [int]$FixedFps = 0, # above 0: every frame advances game time by exactly 1/FixedFps s, whatever the PC's load, so a script gives the same result each run
    [switch]$Packaged, # run the packaged game instead of the uncooked project
    [string]$Exe = "D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe"  # with -Packaged: which packaged game to run
)
if ($Packaged) {
    $exe = $Exe
    $gameArgs = @()
} else {
    $exe = "D:\UE\UE_5.9\Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.exe"
    $gameArgs = @("`"$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Supercut.uproject`"", "-game")
}
# Start-Process joins these with spaces and adds no quotes, so every path is quoted here. The game splits its
# command line with CommandLineToArgvW and FParse::Value reads -Key="a b" (LaunchWindows.cpp, Parse.cpp).
$gameArgs += @(
    "-windowed", "-ResX=$ResX", "-ResY=$ResY", "-WinX=0", "-WinY=0", "-nosplash", "-unattended",
    "`"-SupercutScript=$Script`"", "`"-SupercutShots=$Shots`"", "-SupercutFps",
    "`"-abslog=$Log`""
)
if ($Room) { $gameArgs += "-SupercutRoom=$Room" }
if ($Run) { $gameArgs += "-SupercutRun=$Run" }
if ($Seed -ge 0) { $gameArgs += "-SupercutSeed=$Seed" }
if (-not $NoQuit) { $gameArgs +=

bool FAudioDevice::IsAudioDeviceMuted() const
{
	FAudioDeviceManager* DeviceManager = GEngine->GetAudioDeviceManager();
	if(DeviceManager)
	{
		// Check to see if the device manager has "bPlayAllPIEAudio" enabled
		const bool bIsPlayAllDeviceAudio = DeviceManager->IsPlayAllDeviceAudio();

		// Check if always playing NonRealtime devices, and this is a NonRealtime device
		const bool bIsAlwaysPlayNonRealtime = DeviceManager->IsAlwaysPlayNonRealtimeDeviceAudio() && IsNonRealtime();

		if (bIsPlayAllDeviceAudio || bIsAlwaysPlayNonRealtime)
		{
			return false;
		}

		// If we have one active device, ignore device muting
		if (DeviceManager->GetNumActiveAudioDevices() == 1)
		{
			return false;
		}
	}

	return bIsDeviceMuted;
}

if ($Record) { $gameArgs += "-SupercutRecord=`"$Record`"" }   # quotes after the = so FParse::Value reads a path with spaces
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $gameArgs -PassThru
$null = $p.Handle   # without this PowerShell does not keep the exit code of a process it did not wait on
if (-not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)) {
    # The packaged exe is a launcher with the real game as its child. Stop the child first.
    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ParentProcessId = $($p.Id)" | ForEach-Object {
        Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -Confirm:$false
    }
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force
    Write-Output "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s: the game was stopped"
    exit 3
}
Write-Output "game exit code $($p.ExitCode)"
exit $p.ExitCode

	bool FSoundWavePCMWriter::BeginWriteToWavFile(const TSampleBuffer<>& InSampleBuffer, const FString& FileName, const FString& FilePath, TFunction<void()> OnSuccess)
	{
		if (!IsDone())
		{
			UE_LOGF(LogAudio, Error, "This instance of FSoundWavePCMWriter is already processing another write operation.");
			return false;
		}

		if (!PrepWavFileOutput(InSampleBuffer, FileName, FilePath))
		{
			return false;
		}

		// For convenience in our async task, we only take void(USoundWave*) type lambdas. So let's wrap our void() lambda here:
		TFunction<void(const USoundWave*)> WrappedCallback = [OnSuccess](const USoundWave*)
		{
			OnSuccess();
		};

		CurrentOperation.Reset(new FAsyncSoundWavePCMWriterTask(this, ESoundWavePCMWriteTaskType::WriteWavFile, WrappedCallback));
		CurrentOperation->StartBackgroundTask();

		return true;
	}

	bool FSoundWavePCMWriter::SynchronouslyWriteToWavFile(const TSampleBuffer<>& InSampleBuffer, const FString& FileName, const FString& FilePath, FString* OutFilePathName)
	{
			}
			
			// clear out RawPCMData
			if (Writer->CurrentSoundWave->RawPCMData)
			{
				FMemory::Free(Writer->CurrentSoundWave->RawPCMData);
				Writer->CurrentSoundWave->RawPCMData = nullptr;
			}
		}

		// Capture our callback and perform it on the game thread:
		const USoundWave* SoundWave = Writer->CurrentSoundWave;
		TFunction<void(const USoundWave*)> Callback = MoveTemp(CallbackOnSuccess);

		AsyncTask(ENamedThreads::GameThread, [Callback, SoundWave]() {
			Callback(SoundWave);
		});
	}

	void FAsyncSoundWavePCMWriteWorker::Abandon()
	{
		FScopeLock AbandonLock(&NonAbandonableSection);

		// Do any state cleanup here.
		Writer->CurrentState = ESoundWavePCMWriterState::Cancelled;
	}

"""Read every built WAV back and check it against the rules and its own targets.

    python -I D:\\UE\\Projects\\Supercut59\\Audio\\src\\measure.py

Rules for every file: 48 kHz, 16-bit, mono (stereo where registered), true peak <= -1.0 dBTP,
no DC offset, first and last samples near zero (one-shots), seamless join (loops),
not harsh (<= 15 % of energy above 6 kHz), not thin (spectral flatness >= 0.01 unless the sound
is a deliberate tone). Per-sound targets come from the checks= of each @sound.
Families: variants within 1.5 dB of each other and measurably different (cross-correlation < 0.95).

import numpy as np

SR = dsp.SR


def read(path):
    sr, pcm = wavfile.read(path)
    return sr, pcm, pcm.astype(np.float64) / 32768.0


def mono(x):
    return x if x.ndim == 1 else x.mean(axis=1)


def rms_env(x, win):
    m = mono(x)
    n = len(m) // win
    return np.sqrt(np.mean(m[:n * win].reshape(n, win) ** 2, axis=1) + 1e-20)


def attack_ms(x):
    """Rise time of the first transient: from the first 0.25 ms block above -20 dB of the file's peak
    to the first block within 3 dB of the loudest block in the 30 ms after that onset.
    (A click-clack is judged on its first click, not on the louder clack that follows.)"""
    m = np.abs(mono(x))
    w = max(int(SR * 0.00025), 1)
    k = len(m) // w
    env = m[:k * w].reshape(k, w).max(axis=1)
    onset = int(np.nonzero(env >= env.max() * 0.1)[0][0])
    win = env[onset:onset + int(0.030 / (w / SR))]
    first = int(np.nonzero(win >= win.max() * 0.708)[0][0])
    return first * w / SR * 1000


def gone_by(x):
    """Last time the 5 ms RMS is within 40 dB of its loudest."""
    env = rms_env(x, int(SR * 0.005))
    above = np.nonzero(20 * np.log10(env / env.max()) > -40)[0]
    return (above[-1] + 1) * 0.005


def spectrum(x):
    m = mono(x)
    P = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(m * np.hanning(len(m)))) ** 2
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(len(m), 1 / SR)
    return f, P


def centroid(x):
    f, P = spectrum(x)
    return float((f * P).sum() / P.sum())

for k, (a, b) in enumerate(snap_windows):\n        inside = (t >= a) & (t + 0.1 <= b)\n        rows.append({\"snap\": k + 1, \"loudest_100ms_LUFS\": round(float(lk[inside].max()), 1)})\n    outside = loop's join in still.wav.\n    rec = recs[\"still\"]\n    rows = log_times(os.path.join(log_dir, \"aw_rec_still.log\"))\n    start = next(t for t, line in rows if \"MUSIC start action flat, from bar a)   # one set of gains across the join\n    resid = rec[a:join + SR] - music\n    rms20 = np.sqrt(np.convolve(resid.mean(axis=1) ** 2, np.ones(h) / h, mode=\"valid\"))\n    jr = join - a\n    at_join = float(rms20[jr - h:jr + h].max())\n    typical = float(np.percentile(rms20[:jr - SR], 99))\n    lev = rec.mean(axis=1)\n    c2 = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(lev * lev)])\n\n    def change(i):\n ## 3. Notes for the helper wiring these into the game

**Volume.** Levels are baked into the files. Play every sound at volume 1.0 and they sit right against each other.
Scale only where the table says so (`crate_thud` by impact speed). If the clapper snap does not stand out enough in a
busy fight, lower the other sounds together with a sound class; the clapper file already has 9 dB of peak limiting
and cannot go louder (see section 5).

**Live time, frozen time, both.** The `state` field in `manifest.json` says which.


Nothing on the list was skipped. All 47 named sounds exist, with the variant counts asked for. These are the weak
points.

- **The clapper is not much louder than the rest.** By L100 it is -18.8, 1.2 dB above most one-shots at -20, and
  4 dB under the revolver. By standard LUFS-M (-24.9) it reads quieter than many sounds, because it is so short. It
  already has 9 dB of peak limiting; more would flatten the snap. If it needs to stand out, the fix is to lower
  everything else in the mix, not to push this file.
- **The revolver may read as a drum.** The hearing tool ranks a single shot closest to "a drum hit". A sequence of
  shots does get Gunshot and Cap gun tags. A gunshot is hard to synthesise from scratch: real ones get much of their
  character from the room and the mechanism. `[taste: owner review]`
- **Footsteps and land may read as knocks or a clock.** Alone they score as drum hits; in a walking sequence, as a
  clock first and footsteps third. Real footsteps have heel and toe and a shoe-sole squeak, which I only partly built.

void FMixerDevice::Get2DChannelMap(bool bIsVorbis, const int32 NumSourceChannels, const int32 NumOutputChannels, const bool bIsCenterChannelOnly, Audio::FAlignedFloatBuffer& OutChannelMap)
	{
		if (NumSourceChannels <= 0 ||
			NumOutputChannels <= 0 ||
			NumSourceChannels > AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS || 
			NumOutputChannels > AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS
			)
		{
			// Return a zero'd channel map buffer in the case of an unsupported channel configuration
			OutChannelMap.AddZeroed(AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS * AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS);

#if !NO_LOGGING			
			// Anti-Spam warning.
			static uint64 TimeOfLastLogMsgInCycles = 0;
			constexpr double MinTimeBetweenWarningsInMs = 5000.f; // 5 Secs.
			double ElapsedTimeInMs = FPlatformTime::ToMilliseconds64(FPlatformTime::Cycles64() - TimeOfLastLogMsgInCycles);

			if (ElapsedTimeInMs > MinTimeBetweenWarningsInMs)
			{
				TimeOfLastLogMsgInCycles = FPlatformTime::Cycles64();
				UE_LOGF(LogAudioMixer, Warning, "Unsupported source channel (%d) count or output channels (%d)", NumSourceChannels, NumOutputChannels);
			}	
#endif //!NO_LOGGING
			
			// Bail.
			return;
		}

		// 5.1 Vorbis files have a non-standard channel order so pick a channel map from the 5.1 vorbis channel maps based on the output channels
		if (bIsVorbis && NumSourceChannels == 6)
		{
			OutChannelMap = VorbisChannelMapCache[NumOutputChannels - 1];
		}
		else
		{
			const int32 CacheID = GetChannelMapCacheId(NumSourceChannels, NumOutputChannels, bIsCenterChannelOnly);
			OutChannelMap = ChannelMapCache[CacheID];
		}
	}

void FMixerDevice::InitializeChannelMaps()
	{	
		// If we haven't yet created the static channel map cache
		if (!ChannelMapCache.Num())
		{
			// Make a matrix big enough for every possible configuration, double it to account for center channel only 
			ChannelMapCache.AddZeroed(AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS * AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS * 2);

			// Create a vorbis channel map cache
			VorbisChannelMapCache.AddZeroed(AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS);

			// Loop through all input to output channel map configurations and cache them
			for (int32 OutputChannelCount = 1; OutputChannelCount < AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS + 1; ++OutputChannelCount)
			{
				for (int32 InputChannelCount = 1; InputChannelCount < AUDIO_MIXER_MAX_OUTPUT_CHANNELS + 1; ++InputChannelCount)
				{
					// Cache non-vorbis channel maps
					CacheChannelMap(InputChannelCount, OutputChannelCount, true /* bIsCenterChannelOnly */);
					CacheChannelMap(InputChannelCount, OutputChannelCount, false /* bIsCenterChannelOnly */);
				}
				// Cache vorbis channel maps. 
				bool bSuccess = CreateVorbis2DChannelMap(OutputChannelCount, EChannelMapOrder::OutputMajorOrder, VorbisChannelMapCache[OutputChannelCount - 1]);
				check(bSuccess);
			}
		}
	}

	EqualPower,

	// The mono channel is split 1.0 left/right

78	def events(rows):
79	    """Snaps (with the cue and frame the music was cut at) and resumes (with the cue and bar it came back from)."""
80	    snaps, resumes = [], []
81	    for i, (t, line) in enumerate(rows):
82	        soon = [r[1] for r in rows[i:] if r[0] - t < 0.3]   # what the music did in the 0.3 s after
83	        if "FREEZE begin" in line:
84	            m = next((m for m in (re.search(r"MUSIC cut (\w+) at frame (\d+)", r) for r in soon) if m), None)
85	            snaps.append({"guess": t, "cue": m.group(1) if m else None, "frame": int(m.group(2)) if m else None})
86	        if "FREEZE end" in line:
87	            m = next((m for m in (re.search(r"MUSIC start (\w+) flat, from bar (\d+)", r) for r in soon) if m), None)
88	            resumes.append({"guess": t, "cue": m.group(1) if m else None, "bar": int(m.group(2)) if m else None})
89	    return snaps, resumes

122	def find_hit(rec, around, span=0.3):
123	    """Recording index of freeze_out's hit (its peak, 0.300 s into the file), by matching the file from the hit on."""
124	    sr, pcm = wavfile.read(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "Audio", "wav", "sc_freeze_out.wav"))
125	    f = pcm.astype(np.float64) / 32768.0
126	    hit = int(0.300 * SR)
127	    template = f[hit:hit + int(0.2 * SR)]
128	    lo = around - int(span * SR)
129	    region = rec[lo:around + int(span * SR) + len(template)].mean(axis=1)
130	    c = signal.correlate(region, template, mode="valid", method="fft")
131	    energy = np.sqrt(np.convolve(region * region, np.ones(len(template)), mode="valid")) + 1e-12
132	    k = int(np.argmax(c / energy))
133	    return lo + k, float((c / energy)[k] / np.sqrt(np.sum(template * template)))

136	def loud100(x):
137	    """Every 100 ms window's K-weighted loudness, 10 ms apart, in LUFS."""
138	    ms = dsp._kms(x, int(0.1 * SR), int(0.01 * SR))
139	    return -0.691 + 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(ms, 1e-20))

	/**
	 * A request waits one render more. The audio device starts a sound effect one render (1024 frames) after it is
	 * asked for, while a request runs in the render that comes next: measured in the recordings, the snap landed
	 * 21.3 ms after the music stopped and freeze_out's hit 21.3 ms after the music came back
	 * (Tools\\measure_recordings.py). Held one render, music and effects asked for on one game frame land together.

	void HoldRequestsOneRender() { bHoldOneRender = true; }

('''	TMpscQueue<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Requests;
''',
'''	TMpscQueue<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Requests;
	TArray<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Held;   // with bHoldOneRender: the requests the next render runs
	bool bHoldOneRender = false;
'''),
]

**Fri 13 Nov 15:19:46 · Tool call: Bash** (Find which cue frame is playing at several fight recording times)

```
cd /d/UE/Projects/Supercut59 && cat > "C:/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/ce66ae306241b5fa/f8d28d42-bb09-4411-8a06-883ee052b8a0/scratchpad/probe_frame.py" <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, r'D:/UE/Projects/Supercut59/Tools'); sys.argv=['x']
import measure_recordings as m, numpy as np
from scipy import signal
SR=m.SR
rec=m.read(r'[notes]/unreal/megajam-2026/lanes/audiowire/recordings/fight.wav')
full=sum(m.STEMS['action']).mean(axis=1)  # one pass of the cue
full=np.concatenate([full, full[:2*SR]])
for t in (6.0, 8.0, 8.7, 9.0, 9.5, 10.0, 12.0, 15.1, 15.5, 16.0):
    y=rec[int(t*SR):int((t+0.8)*SR)].mean(axis=1)
    c=signal.correlate(full,y,mode='valid',method='fft')
    e=np.sqrt(np.convolve(full*full,np.ones(len(y)),mode='valid'))+1e-12
    r=c/e/np.sqrt(np.sum(y*y))
    k=int(np.argmax(r)); 
    print('rec %.2f s -> cue frame %d (bar %.3f) score %.2f ; bar start at rec %.4f'%(t,k,k/m.BAR+1,r[k], t-(k%m.BAR)/SR))
EOF

void USoundWave::SetSoundAssetCompressionType(ESoundAssetCompressionType InSoundAssetCompressionType, bool bMarkDirty)
{
#if WITH_EDITOR

	
	/*
	 * This is a bit of a hack to make viable for a hot-fixable.
	 * If bMarkDirty is False and the current compression type is project defined,
	 * it means the project default codec was changed.  In this scenario we don't want
	 * to change the SoundAssetCompressionType field, as this will change the property
	 * on the USoundWave to whatever the new project default is.
	 */
	if(bMarkDirty || SoundAssetCompressionType != ESoundAssetCompressionType::ProjectDefined)
	{
		SoundAssetCompressionType = InSoundAssetCompressionType;
	}

	FName RuntimeFormat = GetWorkingSoundWaveData()->FindRuntimeFormat(*this);
	if (RuntimeFormat.IsNone())
	{
		RuntimeFormat = Audio::ToName(SoundAssetCompressionType);
	}

	GetWorkingSoundWaveData()->CacheRuntimeFormatDependentState(RuntimeFormat);

	UpdateAsset(bMarkDirty);
#endif // #if WITH_EDITOR
}

import glob, re, datetime
def ts(l):
    m=re.match(r'\[(\d{4})\.(\d\d)\.(\d\d)-(\d\d)\.(\d\d)\.(\d\d):(\d{3})\]\[\s*(\d+)\]',l)
    return datetime.datetime(*map(int,m.groups()[:6]),int(m.group(7))*1000) if m else None
for f in sorted(glob.glob('aw_*.log')):
    start=None; n=0; out=[]
    for l in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='replace'):
        if 'START freeze_out' in l:
            start=(ts(l),'from 0.30' in l); n+=1
        elif 'STOP freeze_out' in l and start:
            out.append('%s%.2f'%('S' if start[1] else 'n',(ts(l)-start[0]).total_seconds())); start=None
    if out: print(f, ' '.join(out))
EOF

		// The non-real-time device renders a fixed time per engine tick unless told otherwise. Here it renders

void USupercutAudio::PumpNonRealtime()
{
	FAudioDevice* Device = GetWorld() ? GetWorld()->GetAudioDeviceRaw() : nullptr;
	if (!Device)
	{
		return;
	}
	Audio::FMixerDevice* Mixer = static_cast<Audio::FMixerDevice*>(Device);
	static_cast<Audio::FMixerPlatformNonRealtime*>(Mixer->GetAudioMixerPlatform())->RenderAudio(FApp::GetDeltaTime());
}

    python -I D:\\UE\\Projects\\Supercut59\\Tools\\measure_recordings.py <recordings folder> <logs folder> <out folder>

Reads <name>.wav with its game log aw_rec_<name>.log (fight, still, puzzle, upgrade). The recording mixes music and
sound effects, so the music is measured by fitting the music files to the recording (least squares, one gain per
stem) at the place cross-correlation finds them. For each snap: the music's level in the 100 ms before and after.

```
explicit FSupercutMusicMixer(TSharedRef<const FSupercutMusicTracks> InTracks);

	/** Queues a request from any thread. The render that comes next (the one after, with HoldRequestsOneRender) runs it first, in order. */
	void Enqueue(TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)> Request) { Requests.Enqueue(MoveTemp(Request)); }
	/**
	 * A request waits one render more. The audio device starts a sound effect one render (1024 frames) after it is
	 * asked for, while a request runs in the render that comes next: measured in the recordings, the snap landed
	 * 21.3 ms after the music stopped and freeze_out's hit 21.3 ms after the music came back
	 * (Tools\measure_recordings.py). Held one render, music and effects asked for on one game frame land together.
	 * Call before the first render.
	 */
	void HoldRequestsOneRender() { bHoldOneRender = true; }

	// ---- Requests. Call them through Enqueue unless on the thread that renders.

	void FadeOutMain(int64 FadeFrames);
	void Publish();

	TSharedRef<const FSupercutMusicTracks> Tracks;
	TMpscQueue<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Requests;
	TArray<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Held;   // with bHoldOneRender: the requests the next render runs
	bool bHoldOneRender = false;
	FVoice Main;
	FVoice Old;   // the cue a bar-line change or a stop is fading out
	FStinger Stinger;
	Volume = InVolume;
}

void FSupercutMusicMixer::Render(float* Out, int32 Frames)
{
	TArray<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Due = MoveTemp(Held);
	Held.Reset();
	while (TOptional<TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>> Request = Requests.Dequeue())
	{
		(bHoldOneRender ? Held : Due).Add(MoveTemp(*Request));
	}
	for (TUniqueFunction<void(FSupercutMusicMixer&)>& Request : Due)
	{
		Request(*this);
	}
		USoundSubmix& Main = Device->GetMainSubmixObject();
		Main.OnSubmixRecordedFileDone.AddDynamic(this, &USupercutAudio::OnRecordingWritten);
		UAudioMixerBlueprintLibrary::StartRecordingOutput(&InWorld, 300.f, &Main);
		bRecording = true;
		UE_LOG(LogSupercutSound, Display, TEXT("SOUND recording the master output to %s"), *RecordPath);
	}
#endif

	Music->HoldRequestsOneRender();
	MusicComponent = NewObject<USupercutMusicComponent>(InWorld.GetWorldSettings());
	MusicComponent->SetMixer(Music.ToSharedRef());
	MusicComponent->RegisterComponent();
	MusicComponent->SetVolumeMultiplier(SoundUnderClapper);   // after RegisterComponent, which makes the audio component this sets
	MusicComponent->Start();
}

 "old_string": "def share(rec, cue, frame, start, n, gains):\n    \"\"\"How much of the music, the cue's stems from frame `frame` at `gains`, rec[start:start+n] holds: 1 all of it,\n    0 none. One fixed shape is projected, so a loud sound effect over the window barely moves it, where a fit\n    with a free gain per stem takes part of the effect for music.\"\"\"\n    music = sum(g * c for g, c in zip(gains, stems_at(cue, frame, n))).reshape(-1)\n    return float(np.dot(rec[start:start + n].reshape(-1), music) / np.dot(music, music))",
 "new_string": "def placed(name, at, i, start, n):\n    \"\"\"sc_<name>.wav laid on the recording's timeline with its point `at` s at index i, cut to [start, start+n).\"\"\"\n    sr, pcm = wavfile.read(os.path.join(HERE, \"..\", \"Audio\", \"wav\", \"sc_\" + name + \".wav\"))\n    f = pcm.astype(np.float64) / 32768.0\n    f = np.stack([f, f], axis=1) if f.ndim == 1 else f\n    out = np.zeros((n, 2))\n    first = i - int(at * SR)   # recording index of the file's first frame\n    a, b = max(start, first), min(start + n, first + len(f))\n    if a < b:\n        out[a - start:b - start] = f[a - first:b - first]\n    return out\n\n\ndef share(rec, cue, frame, start, n, gains, effects):\n    \"\"\"How much of the music, the cue's stems from frame `frame` at `gains`, rec[start:start+n] holds: 1 all of it,\n    0 none. The music is one fixed shape, fitted together with the flat sound effects the event starts\n    (`effects`: (name, at, i) for placed()), each with a gain of its own. A loud effect would otherwise pass for music\n    by chance.\"\"\"\n    music = sum(g * c for g, c in zip(gains, stems_at(cue, frame, n))).reshape(-1)\n    A = np.stack([music] + [placed(e, at, i, start, n).reshape(-1) for e, at, i in effects], axis=1)\n    coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, rec[start:start + n].reshape(-1), rcond=None)\n    return float(coef[0])"
}
