cd "[notes]/unreal" && cat >> GOTCHAS.md <<'EOF'

## SUPERCUT audiowire lane (13 Nov 2026, c4, engine 5.9 preview)

- **Quitting before the engine has written a recording crashes the exit** (13 Nov 2026, verified).
  `UAudioMixerBlueprintLibrary::StopRecordingOutput...` hands the file to a game-thread callback, and the writer lives
  in a static (`RecordingData`) that the callback frees. Quit before it runs and the exit fails with 0xC0000005 after
  "Exiting.". Pass the main submix to Start and Stop explicitly, bind `USoundSubmix::OnSubmixRecordedFileDone` (it is
  only broadcast when a submix was passed) and quit after it fires. Seen once more on 13 Nov with this in place, in 1 of
  2 runs of the same script, after the file was written; no crash report was left, cause unknown.
- **A flat mono sound plays at -3 dB per side by default** (13 Nov 2026, verified in source and by measurement).
  `UAudioSettings::MonoChannelUpmixMethod` defaults to Linear (0.5 per side). EqualPower gives 0.707 per side. Set it
  in `[/Script/Engine.AudioSettings]` in DefaultEngine.ini; the mixer reads it once at device init
  (AudioMixerDevice.cpp, FMixerDevice init).
- **`USynthComponent::SetVolumeMultiplier` before `RegisterComponent` does nothing** (13 Nov 2026, verified in source).
  OnRegister makes the inner audio component the call sets. Call it after RegisterComponent.
- **A new one-shot starts one device buffer after it is asked for** (13 Nov 2026, verified by measurement). With the
  offline renderer, a sound played on a game frame starts 1024 frames (21.3 ms at 48 kHz) later, while a request
  queued to a SynthComponent runs in its very next render (512 frames per call). `FAudioDevice::GetBufferLength()`
  returns that 1024 (CallbackBufferFrameSize). Holding the synth's requests 1024 frames lines them up: the snap and
  the music cut now measure 0.0 ms apart. The realtime device was not measured.
- **`-NonRealtimeAudio`: a sound started part way into its file can start hundreds of ms late** (13 Nov 2026,
  verified). A start time above 0 forces realtime decoding and an async first decode (AudioMixerSource.cpp,
  PrepareForInitialization and IsPreparedToInit); the source waits for that task. Once in about 25 plays, under load,
  it started 340 ms late. `-DeterministicAudio` (new in 5.9) uses the same offline renderer, decodes synchronously
  and runs without the audio thread (AudioMixerSourceDecode.cpp `ShouldForceSyncDecode`, AudioDeviceManager.cpp).
  `IsNonRealtime()` is true for it too, so code that pumps the non-realtime device works unchanged.
- **Under an offline audio device the log clock and the recording drift apart** (13 Nov 2026, verified). The
  recording holds the audio rendered; nothing renders during start-up or a room load while the wall clock runs on.

def lufs_i(x, loop=False):
    """Integrated loudness with the absolute (-70) and relative (-10) gates, in LUFS."""
    ms = _kms(x, n_of(0.4), n_of(0.1), loop)
    lk = -0.691 + 10 * np.log10(np.maximum(ms, 1e-20))
    g = ms[lk > -70]
    if not len(g):
        return -99.0
    rel = -0.691 + 10 * np.log10(g.mean()) - 10
    g2 = ms[(lk > -70) & (lk > rel)]
    return -0.691 + 10 * np.log10(g2.mean())

**Heat.** Drive the heat stem's gain from 0 to 1 when the room gets hot (for example 3 or more enemies alive, or the
player hurt in the last few seconds). Fade it in over about one bar (1.7 s) and out over about two. At 1.0 it adds
1.2 LU (the full mix goes from -20.0 to -18.8 LUFS-I). The four stems summed at 1.0 peak at -2.82 dBTP, so they
cannot clip.

**Switching cues.** All cues share tempo and key, so a change can wait for the next bar line of the playing cue
(a 1.67 s wait at most) and start the new cue at its bar 1. Fight to puzzle, title to take start, and so on, all
land in time. A short cross-fade (50 to 100 ms) on that bar line is enough.

How the files get into the game, and how to add one\n\nSound effects:\n\n1. `Audio\\wav\\sc_<name>.wav` (or `sc_<name>_1..N.wav` for variants), listed in `Audio\\wav\\manifest.json`.\n2. `Tools\\make_sounds.py` imports each one as `/Game/Audio/sc_<name>`: deleted and made again on each run, PCM\n   (no lossy codec), looping for the manifest's loops, loading behaviour Force Inline. Run it headless:\n\n   ```\n   D:\\UE\\UE_5.9\\Engine\\Binaries\\Win64\\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe D:\\UE\\Projects\\Supercut59\\Supercut.uproject -run=pythonscript -Script=D:\\UE\\Projects\\Supercut59\\Tools\\make_sounds.py -nullrhi -unattended -nopause -nosplash\n   ```\n\n   It ends with one line per sound (name, looping, compression, loading, channels, length); two runs gave the same\n   lines.\n3. `Config/DefaultGame.ini` cooks all of `/Game/Audio`, so a packaged build carries every sound with nothing to list.\n\nMusic: not imported. `SupercutMusic.cpp` reads the 8 WAVs from `Audio\\music\\wav` when the world starts, and\n`Supercut.Build.cs` stages them beside the packaged game. A missing file stops the game with a clear error.\n\nTo add a sound effect:\n\n1. Put the WAV in `Audio\\wav` and its row in `manifest.json`.\n2. Add a row to the table in `USupercutAudio::Cues()` (SupercutAudio.cpp): name, number of files, loop, placed, freeze\n   rule, plays through screens.\n3. Run `make_sounds.py`.\n4. Call `USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayFlat(TEXT(\"name\"))`, `PlayAt`, `PlayOn` or `PlayOnAt` at the event.\n5. Run the tests: `TheTableMatchesTheSoundManifest` fails if the table and the manifest disagree.\n\nTo add a music cue: a value in `ESupercutMusicCue`, its file in `Supercut.Build.cs`'s list and in the loader, and its\nvolume in `FSupercutMusicMixer::CueVolume`.\n\nVolumes from code: `USupercutAudio::Get(this).SetMasterVolume(v)` and `SetMusicVolume(v)`, 0 to 1, both 1 at start.\nThere is no menu.\n\nSound log: category `LogSupercutSound`. Every start and stop is one line: `START <file> flat`, `START <file> placed\n<n> cm`, `STOP <file> flat, played out`, `PAUSE`, `RESUME`. Music lines start with `MUSIC`. Its gains (one per stem) are fitted over a\n  clean second. The \"after\" runs render\nsound offline, not through the speakers; the realtime device was not timed.\n\n## 6. What to check by ear\n\n- **The overall level.** The fight sits at about -32 LUFS integrated, quiet for a game (many sit near -23 to -18).\n  The fight's true peak is -6.87 dBTP, so the master could rise about 5 dB before it nears -1 dBTP.\n  `[taste: owner review]`\n- **The music under the effects.** The action music alone is -35.7 LUFS in game, about 10 dB under the music\n  hand-off's \"about -26\". It follows from the step in section 7 that lowers everything but the clapper by 8 dB.\n- The snap against a revolver shot in a busy moment: it measures 2.3 dB clear, which may or may not read as clearly\n  louder.\n- freeze_out's hit with the music's return after a second clap: measured 21.3 ms apart (one device block) in two of\n  three clap ends. I expect this to sound together; check it.\n- The heat stem coming in when the third enemy appears, and going after the room calms.\n- The frozen bed and the 12 dB duck of the stage bed under it.\n- The Marksman's shot hum at pitch 1.5.\n- The room-clear sting landing on a beat, not a bar line.\n\n## 7. Judgement calls, and what I turned down\n\n- **Everything but the clapper is 8 dB down** (`SoundUnderClapper` 0.4: every effect, the beds and the music;\n  clap_snap, freeze_in and freeze_out stay at 1). The sound hand-off's section 3 says to lower the other sounds\n  together if the snap does not stand out. Before this the snap's loudest 100 ms (-22.9) was quieter than a revolver\n  shot (-19.6).\n- **EqualPower mono upmix.** The engine's default plays every mono effect 3 dB under its file. With EqualPower a flat\n  effect plays at the level the sound lane baked into it.\n- **The music waits one device buffer** (1024 frames, `Device->GetBufferLength()`). A new effect starts one buffer\n  after it is asked for, the music's request in its next render. Held, the snap and the cut land 0.0 ms apart\n  (21.3 ms before).\n- **Recordings and silent runs use `-DeterministicAudio`, not `-NonRealtimeAudio`.** Both render offline. With\n  `-NonRealtimeAudio`, a sound started part way into its file (freeze_out after a second clap) waits for an async\n  decode, and once, under load, its hit came 352 ms after the music. The deterministic device decodes on the spot\n  and has no audio thread. Players get the normal realtime device either way.\n- **freeze_out on a second clap starts 0.30 s into its file**, so its hit (the file's loudest point, at 0.300 s) lands\n  on the resume frame. On a timer end it starts 0.30 s before the end. Scene end plays it the same way as a clap.\n- **Heat is a gain, not a cue change.** It fades in over one bar from the moment the rule turns true, as the music\n  hand-off suggests, instead of waiting for a bar line. The stems never leave sync.\n- **The room-clear sting lands on the next beat**, not the next bar line, so it follows the last kill closely.\n- **Death cuts the music dead**, like the snap, instead of fading it.\n- **rev_reload plays when the reload starts.**\n- **The Marksman's shot hum is the enemy_shot_fly loop at pitch 1.5**, since the table asks for a faster hum on its\n  fast shot. `[pick]`\n- **The stage bed ducks 12 dB under the frozen bed**, the table's first pick.\n- **No sound for a door shutting:** the table has none, so I invented none.\n- **Recording the upgrade screen:** `Script/run.txt` failed 3 times at real speed (36 fps average with stalls while\n  the PC was loaded), so `Script/sound_upgrade.txt` plays run.txt only up to the upgrade screen.\n- Turned down: matplotlib for the spectrograms. Here it fails to import (no fontTools) and I may not install\n  anything, so they are drawn with PIL.\n- Turned down: lowering the resume check's match bar. The upgrade resume fails at 0.468 against 0.5; I report it.\n\n## 8. What failed or was skipped\n\n- **crate_thud** is never played: crates are removed, they never land. No event was invented.\n- **mx_title** is not used: no title screen.\n- **ui_move** plays, but no test covers it.\n- **The upgrade resume check fails** on the match score (section 5).\n- **One exit crash** after a recording was written (0xC0000005 after \"Exiting.\", no crash report), 1 of 2 runs of\n  the upgrade script on the final build. The earlier crash of that kind came from quitting before the engine let go\n  of its recording writer; the game now waits for that, so this one is something else.\n- **Startup ensures** in every run of the uncooked game: `MTAccessDetector.h` line 396, two ensure reports per run\n  in `Saved\\Crashes`. They come from the engine and were there before this lane.\n- **The realtime audio device was not measured.** The speakers were off limits, so every recording is offline. Lag\n  and loudness through the realtime device may differ slightly.\n- **The quiet overall level** is reported, not changed.\n\n## 9. Engine traps\n\nAdded to `unreal\\GOTCHAS.md` under \"SUPERCUT audiowire lane\": the recording writer crash at exit, the -3 dB mono\ndefault, SynthComponent volume before registering, the one-buffer start of a new sound, the late start of a sound\nstarted part way in under `-NonRealtimeAudio`, the log clock drifting from the recording, and the offline device\nplaying on with the window unfocused.\n"
}

void USupercutAudio::OnResumed()
{
	if (!bFreezeOutStarted)
	{
		// The freeze ended early: start freeze_out at its hit, so the hit lands on this frame.
		PlayFlat(TEXT("freeze_out"), SoundFreezeOutLead);
	}
	if (HangsThisFreeze > 0)
	{
		PlayFlat(TEXT("shot_release"));
	}
	HangsThisFreeze = 0;
	SendMusic([](FSupercutMusicMixer& Mixer) { Mixer.Resume(); });

	// The countdown in a freeze, and freeze_out timed so its hit lands as the world resumes.
	if (Time.IsFrozen() && !World->IsPaused())
	{
		const float Remaining = Time.GetFreezeRemaining();
		for (int32 Second = 3; Second >= 1; --Second)
		{
			if (LastRemaining > Second && Remaining <= Second)
			{
				PlayFlat(TEXT("freeze_tick"));
			}
		}
		if (!bFreezeOutStarted && Remaining <= SoundFreezeOutLead)
		{
			PlayFlat(TEXT("freeze_out"));
			bFreezeOutStarted = true;
		}
float FSupercutMusicMixer::CueVolume(ESupercutMusicCue Cue)
{
	switch (Cue)
	{
	case ESupercutMusicCue::Action: return 0.5f;
	case ESupercutMusicCue::Puzzle: return 0.5f;
	case ESupercutMusicCue::Between: return 0.7f;
	case ESupercutMusicCue::None: break;
	}
	return 0.f;
}

That helper found four faults in the code plates that a room file cannot fix. Fix them:

1. **Plates show nothing until the whole code is in.** Today each right plate lights green at once, so a player can find the code by trying plates one at a time and never needs to see the frozen-only marks. New rule: a plate that is hit lights in a neutral colour (white) and counts as entered. When as many plates are entered as the code is long, the stand answers once: all green and the door opens if the order was the code, or a red flash and every plate clears if not. Nothing before that moment tells right from wrong.
2. **A hit on a plate that is already entered does nothing.** Today it counts as wrong and clears the code. With the DOUBLE EXPOSURE upgrade a hung shot comes back as two, the second hits the plate the first one lit, and the meant answer fails with no way for the player to know why.
3. **Shots left hanging in one freeze count in the order they were fired.** Today that holds only for shots that land in the same frame; otherwise the nearest plate counts first. Setting up three shots in a freeze, in code order, and letting them go is the game's own idea, so it must work from anywhere in the room. Hold the plate hits of shots released from one freeze until every shot of that release has landed or gone, or until 0.6 s of scene time after that release's first plate hit, whichever comes first, then count them in firing order. Shots fired in live time count on impact as today. Put the 0.6 in `SupercutTuning.h`.
4. **A room file can set the order of the plates on the stand**: an optional `order=` setting on the `plates` line that lists the symbols left to right. Without it the order is mixed as today. Refuse a line whose order does not hold exactly the stand's symbols. Document it in `lanes\run\HANDOFF.md` section 1.

And two tools:

5. **A switch to start with upgrades held**: `-SupercutUpgrades=<name>,<name>` (the names the PICK log lines use), and a matching parameter on `Tools\run_demo.ps1`, so a room can be tested with an upgrade without playing four rooms first.

/**
 * A row of four plates on a stand. Each shows a symbol all the time. Shooting the plates in the order
 * of the code opens a door for good. A wrong plate clears the progress and flashes every plate red.
 * Plates hit in the same frame count in the order their shots were fired.
 */
UCLASS()
class ASupercutPlates : public AActor
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutPlates();

	/** Call before it begins play. Order is the four symbols left to right as the player sees them. */
	void Setup(const FString& InDoorId, const TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& InCode, const TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& InOrder);

	virtual void BeginPlay() override;
	/** Ticks after every shot of the frame has moved, so it sees all of a frame's hits at once. */
	virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;

	/** A player shot landed on this stand. Only a plate counts; the stand's frame does nothing. */
	void TakeShot(const UPrimitiveComponent* Part, int32 FireNumber);

	/** The refill pad: progress cleared. A solved code stays solved. */
	void ResetPuzzle();

	int32 GetProgress() const { return Progress; }
	bool IsSolved() const { return bSolved; }
	bool IsFlashing() const { return FlashLeft > 0.f; }
	/** The plates' symbols, left to right for a player facing them. */
	const TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& GetOrder() const { return Order; }
	/** The plate showing a symbol, for tests and scripts. */
	UStaticMeshComponent* GetPlate(ESupercutSymbol Symbol) const;

private:
	void HitPlate(int32 Plate);
	void ShowState();

	struct FPendingHit
	{
		int32 FireNumber;
		int32 Plate;
	};

	UPROPERTY()
	TArray<TObjectPtr<UStaticMeshComponent>> Boards;

	UPROPERTY()
	TArray<TObjectPtr<UMaterialInstanceDynamic>> Rims;

	FString DoorId;
	TArray<ESupercutSymbol> Code;
	TArray<ESupercutSymbol> Order;
	TArray<bool> Lit;
	TArray<FPendingHit> Pending;
	int32 Progress = 0;
	float FlashLeft = 0.f;
	bool bSolved = false;
};

*
 * A piece type asks for each setting by name. A setting that is missing, a value that does not
 * parse and a setting nobody asked for all become errors that name the file and the line.
 * Nothing is ever filled in with a default.
 */
class FSupercutPieceReader
{
public:
	FSupercutPieceReader(const FString& InFile, int32 InLine, const FString& InType, const TMap<FString, FString>& InSettings, TArray<FString>& InErrors, TArray<FSupercutRoomNote>& InNotes);

	float Number(const TCHAR* Key);        // 12 or -3.5
	FVector Vector(const TCHAR* Key);      // x,y,z
	FVector2D Point(const TCHAR* Key);     // x,y
	FString Word(const TCHAR* Key);        // one word, lower case
	bool YesNo(const TCHAR* Key);          // yes or no

	/**
	 * Reports something wrong with this line that only the piece type can know.
	 * It says nothing when a setting on this line was already missing or unreadable: such a setting
	 * reads as zero or empty, and a complaint about a value nobody wrote would only mislead.
	 */
	void Fail(const FString& What);

	/** A fact for the whole-room checks (FSupercutRoomRule), kept with this line's number. */
	void Note(const TCHAR* Key, const FString& Value = FString(), int32 Number = 0);

	/** The loader calls this after Read: a setting that was written but never asked for is an error. */
	void FailUnreadSettings();

private:
	void Report(const FString& What);
	const FString* Find(const TCHAR* Key);
	bool Numbers(const TCHAR* Key, int32 Count, const TCHAR* Shape, double* Out);

	const FString& File;
	const int32 Line;

79			Tail->DestroyComponent();
80		}
81		UMaterialInterface* Material = SupercutShapes::Glow(this, Color, Strength);
82		Core = SupercutShapes::Add(this, RootComponent, ESupercutShape::Sphere, FVector::ZeroVector, FRotator::ZeroRotator, FVector(CoreSize), Material);
83		// The cone's tip is +Z. Pitch 90 turns +Z to -X, so the tip trails behind the core.
84		Tail = SupercutShapes::Add(this, RootComponent, ESupercutShape::Cone, FVector(-TailLength * 0.5f, 0.f, 0.f), FRotator(90.f, 0.f, 0.f), FVector(TailWidth, TailWidth, TailLength), Material);
85		Core->SetCastShadow(false);
86		Tail->SetCastShadow(false);
87	}

/**
 * A row of four plates on a stand. Each shows a symbol all the time. Shooting the plates in the order
 * of the code opens a door for good. A wrong plate clears the progress and flashes every plate red.
 * Plates hit in the same frame count in the order their shots were fired.
 */
UCLASS()
class ASupercutPlates : public AActor
{
	GENERATED_BODY()

public:
	ASupercutPlates();

	/** Call before it begins play. Order is the four symbols left to right as the player sees them. */
	void Setup(const FString& InDoorId, const TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& InCode, const TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& InOrder);

	virtual void BeginPlay() override;
	/** Ticks after every shot of the frame has moved, so it sees all of a frame's hits at once. */
	virtual void Tick(float DeltaSeconds) override;

	/** A player shot landed on this stand. Only a plate counts; the stand's frame does nothing. */
	void TakeShot(const UPrimitiveComponent* Part, int32 FireNumber);

	/** The refill pad: progress cleared. A solved code stays solved. */
	void ResetPuzzle();

	int32 GetProgress() const { return Progress; }
	bool IsSolved() const { return bSolved; }
	bool IsFlashing() const { return FlashLeft > 0.f; }
	/** The plates' symbols, left to right for a player facing them. */

// plates door=id at=x,y,z facing=degrees code=symbol,symbol,symbol
// Four plates on a stand. at is the stand's floor point and facing the way the plates face. The code is
// 2 to 4 symbols with no repeats; plates for other symbols make up four. Their order is mixed from the
// line itself, so it is the same on every run.
static FSupercutPieceType GPlatesPiece(TEXT("plates"), ESupercutPieceCount::Any, [](FSupercutPieceReader& In) -> FSupercutPieceBuild
{
	const FString DoorId = In.Word(TEXT("door"));
	const FVector At = In.Vector(TEXT("at"));
	const float Facing = In.Number(TEXT("facing"));
	const FString CodeText = In.Word(TEXT("code"));

	TArray<FString> Words;
	CodeText.ParseIntoArray(Words, TEXT(","), false);
	TArray<ESupercutSymbol> Code;
	for (const FString& Word : Words)
	{
		ESupercutSymbol Symbol;
		if (!PuzzleFindSymbol(Word, Symbol))
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("code=%s: \"%s\" is not a symbol. The symbols are: %s"), *CodeText, *Word, *PuzzleAllSymbolNames()));
		}
		else if (Code.Contains(Symbol))
		{
			In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("code=%s uses %s twice. A code has no repeats"), *CodeText, *Word));
		}
		else
		{
			Code.Add(Symbol);
		}
	}
	if (!CodeText.IsEmpty() && (Words.Num() < 2 || Words.Num() > 4))
	{
		In.Fail(FString::Printf(TEXT("code=%s: a code has 2 to 4 symbols and this one has %d"), *CodeText, Words.Num()));
	}
	In.Note(TEXT("door user"), DoorId);
	In.Note(TEXT("code"), CodeText);

	// The plates: the code's symbols and others to make four, mixed by a stream seeded from this line.
	TArray<ESupercutSymbol> Order = Code;
	if (Code.Num() == Words.Num() && Code.Num() >= 2 && Code.Num() <= 4)
	{
		FRandomStream Mix(int32(FCrc::StrCrc32(*FString::Printf(TEXT("%s %s %.0f,%.0f,%.0f %.0f"), *DoorId, *CodeText, At.X, At.Y, At.Z, Facing))));
		auto Shuffle = [&Mix](TArray<ESupercutSymbol>& Symbols)
		{
			for (int32 Index = Symbols.Num() - 1; Index > 0; --Index)
			{
				Symbols.Swap(Index, Mix.RandRange(0, Index));
			}
		};
		TArray<ESupercutSymbol> Others;
		for (const FPuzzleSymbolName& Known : PuzzleSymbolNames)
		{
			if (!Code.Contains(Known.Symbol))
			{
				Others.Add(Known.Symbol);
			}
		}
		Shuffle(Others);
		Order.Append(Others.GetData(), 4 - Code.Num());

	// Up to three upgrades the player does not hold, in an order the seed decides.
	TArray<FName> Pool;
	for (const FSupercutUpgrade& Upgrade : SupercutUpgrades::All())
	{
		if (!Held.Contains(Upgrade.Key))
		{
			Pool.Add(Upgrade.Key);
		}
	}
	Offer.Reset();
	while (Offer.Num() < OfferSize && Pool.Num() > 0)
	{
		const int32 Index = Random.RandRange(0, Pool.Num() - 1);
		Offer.Add(Pool[Index]);
		Pool.RemoveAt(Index);
	}
	if (Offer.Num() == 0)
	{
		UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK skipped: every upgrade is held"));
		EnterRoom(RoomIndex + 1, false);
		return;
	}

	TArray<FString> Names;
	for (const FName Key : Offer)
	{
		Names.Add(Key.ToString());
	}
	SetPhase(ESupercutRunPhase::Picking);
	SetPaused(true);
	Audio.PlayFlat(TEXT("ui_open"));
	Audio.MusicPlay(ESupercutMusicCue::Between);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK offered: %s"), *FString::Join(Names, TEXT(", ")));
}

bool USupercutRun::Pick(int32 OfferIndex)
{
	checkf(Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Picking, TEXT("USupercutRun::Pick: no upgrade screen is open"));
	if (!Offer.IsValidIndex(OfferIndex))
	{
		return false;
	}
	const FName Key = Offer[OfferIndex];
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("PICK taken: card %d, %s"), OfferIndex + 1, *Key.ToString());
	Offer.Reset();
	USupercutAudio::Get(this).PlayFlat(TEXT("ui_pick"));
	Grant(Key);
	SetPaused(false);
	EnterRoom(RoomIndex + 1, false);
	return true;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Takes and rooms

void USupercutRun::Begin(const TArray<FString>& InRoomNames, int32 Seed)
{
	checkf(Phase == ESupercutRunPhase::Idle, TEXT("USupercutRun::Begin: a run is on already"));
	checkf(InRoomNames.Num() > 0, TEXT("USupercutRun::Begin: the run has no rooms"));
	for (const FString& Name : InRoomNames)
	{
		SupercutRoomFile::LoadOrDie(Name);
	}
	RoomNames = InRoomNames;
	Random.Initialize(Seed);
	Take = 1;
	Stats = FSupercutRunStats();
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("RUN begins: %d rooms (%s), seed %d"), RoomNames.Num(), *FString::Join(RoomNames, TEXT(", ")), Seed);
	StartTake();
}

void USupercutRun::StartTake()
{
	Held.Reset();
	SupercutUpgrades::ApplyRules(*this);
	const USupercutTime& Time = USupercutTime::Get(this);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("TAKE %d begins: %d upgrades held, freezes last %.1f s, the board holds %d charges"), Take, Held.Num(), Time.GetFreezeLength(), Time.GetMaxCharges());
	EnterRoom(0, true);
}

int32 USupercutRun::LeaveRoom()

	USupercutTime::Get(this).EndScene();

		Shot->Destroy();

	}

void USupercutRun::Grant(FName Key)
{
	const FSupercutUpgrade* Upgrade = SupercutUpgrades::Find(Key);
	checkf(Upgrade, TEXT("USupercutRun::Grant: there is no upgrade \"%s\""), *Key.ToString());
	checkf(!Held.Contains(Key), TEXT("USupercutRun::Grant: \"%s\" is held already"), *Key.ToString());
	Held.Add(Key);
	SupercutUpgrades::ApplyRules(*this);
	UE_LOG(LogSupercut, Display, TEXT("UPGRADE gained: %s, \"%s\" (%d held)"), Upgrade->Name, *Upgrade->Fact(FSupercutTuning::Get()), Held.Num());
}

# Runs the scripted player in a real game window and waits for it to quit.
# Default: the uncooked project through the editor exe. With -Packaged: the packaged game.
# Usage: powershell -File Tools\run_demo.ps1 [-Shots <folder>] [-ResX 1280] [-ResY 720] [-Script <file>]
#        [-Room <name>] [-Run <name>] [-Seed <n>] [-Log <file>] [-TimeoutSeconds 240] [-NoQuit] [-Packaged [-Exe <packaged Supercut.exe>]]
#        [-FixedFps <n>] [-Silent] [-Record <file.wav>]
# Exit code: 0 the script finished, 2 the script failed (the player died when the script did not expect it,
# or a "scene" step did not see its room), 3 the game was stopped at the timeout.
param(
    [string]$Shots = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\shots",
    [int]$ResX = 1280,
    [int]$ResY = 720,
    [string]$Script = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Script\demo.txt",
    [string]$Room = "",   # play one room, Content\Rooms\<name>.txt, as a run of its own
    [string]$Run = "",    # play the run list Content\Runs\<name>.txt instead of main.txt
    [int]$Seed = -1,      # the seed that decides which upgrades are offered; -1 leaves it to the game
    [string]$Log = "$(Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot)\Saved\Logs\demo.log",
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 240,
    [switch]$NoQuit,   # leave out -SupercutQuit: the game keeps running after the script and is stopped at the timeout
    [int]$FixedFps = 0, # above 0: every frame advances game time by exactly 1/FixedFps s, whatever the PC's load, so a script gives the same result each run
    [switch]$Packaged, # run the packaged game instead of the uncooked project
    [string]$Exe = "D:\UE\Builds\Supercut59\Windows\Supercut.exe",  # with -Packaged: which packaged game to run
    [switch]$Silent,   # render the sound without sending it to the speakers (the engine's deterministic offline audio device)
    [string]$Record = ""  # write the master output to this .wav (also silent); record at real speed, without -FixedFps
)
if ($Packaged) {
    $exe = $Exe

} else {

struct FPuzzleTestWorld : FTestWorldWrapper
	{
		bool Start()
		{
			if (!CreateTestWorld(EWorldType::Game))
			{
				return false;
			}
			GetTestWorld()->GetWorldSettings()->DefaultGameMode = AGameModeBase::StaticClass();
			return BeginPlayInTestWorld();
		}

		void Tick(float Seconds)
		{
			const int32 Ticks = FMath::RoundToInt(Seconds / PuzzleTestStep);
			for (int32 Index = 0; Index < Ticks; ++Index)
			{
				TickTestWorld(PuzzleTestStep);
			}
		}

		USupercutRun& Run() { return USupercutRun::Get(GetTestWorld()); }
		USupercutTime& Time() { return USupercutTime::Get(GetTestWorld()); }
		ASupercutCharacter* Hero() { return Run().GetHero(); }

		template <typename T>
		T* Find()
		{
			TActorIterator<T> It(GetTestWorld());
			return It ? *It : nullptr;
		}

		ASupercutDoor* Door(const FString& Id)
		{
			for (TActorIterator<ASupercutDoor> It(GetTestWorld()); It; ++It)
			{
				if (It->GetId() == Id)
				{
					return *It;
				}
			}
			return nullptr;
		}

		/** A player shot that starts at From and flies straight at Target. */
		ASupercutShot* Fire(const FVector& From, const FVector& Target)
		{
			FActorSpawnParameters Params;
			Params.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;
			ASupercutShot* Shot = GetTestWorld()->SpawnActor<ASupercutShot>(From, FRotator::ZeroRotator, Params);
			Shot->Launch(Hero(), true, (Target - From).GetSafeNormal() * FSupercutTuning::Get().ShotSpeed, 0.f);
			return Shot;
		}

		/** A shot made now, launched later: the order of Launch calls is the firing order. */
		ASupercutShot* Load(const FVector& From)
		{
			FActorSpawnParameters Params;
			Params.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;
			return GetTestWorld()->SpawnActor<ASupercutShot>(From, FRotator::ZeroRotator, Params);
		}

		void ToGateAndWait()

179	A mark on a wall, 90 high, with `n` pips under it, that shows only in frozen time. It has no collision.
180	`at` is the symbol's centre, a little in front of the wall. `facing` points out of the wall.
181	`order` is 1, 2, 3 or 4. The glyphs of a room, read by their order, must give the code of every

184	**`switch door=<id> at=x,y,z facing=degrees seconds=s`**
185	A round target, 90 across, with a ring of 16 segments. `at` is its centre and `facing` the way it
186	faces. A player shot opens the door for `seconds` of scene time. The ring lights green and empties

## 1. How to write a room

A room is one text file in `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut\Content\Rooms`. Its name is the file name without
`.txt`. The file `soundstage.txt` there is the full test room and a good one to copy from.

### The rules of the file

- One piece per line. The first word is the piece type. After it come settings written `key=value`.
- Settings are split by spaces. A value never holds a space: write `from=0,-400,0`, not `from=0, -400, 0`.
- Settings can come in any order. Extra spaces between them are fine, so columns can be lined up.
- `#` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. Blank lines are fine.
- Every setting a piece type lists is required. Nothing has a default. A setting the type does not
  know is an error.
- Lines can come in any order. One thing depends on order: enemies of every kind (`grunt`, `rusher`,
  `marksman`) share one numbering, 0, 1, 2 in the order their lines appear. The scripted player's
  `aim <n>` and the log lines (`RUSHER 1 winds up`) use that number. (Enemies lane, 13 Nov 2026.)
249:- To put the room in the run, add its name on its own line in `Content\Runs\main.txt`, or write
250:  another list in `Content\Runs` and start with `-SupercutRun=<list name>`.
415:- The run list is `Content\Runs\main.txt`: one room name per line.
431:- `-SupercutRun=<name>` plays `Content\Runs\<name>.txt`.
648:RUN list read: 3 rooms (soundstage, proproom, backlot) from D:/UE/Builds/Supercut/Windows/Supercut/Content/Runs/main.txt
775:- **`-SupercutRoom` and `-SupercutRun` take a name, not a path.** Turned down: full paths. Names

```
## 4. How the run works

`USupercutRun` (a world subsystem, `SupercutRun.h`) owns the room and the player's character.

- The run list is `Content\Runs\main.txt`: one room name per line.
- Entering a room: the old room, its pieces and every shot are destroyed, a freeze in progress is
  ended, the next room is built from its file, charges go to the most the board holds, and the
  player is put on the start. The HUD shows `SCENE n` and `TAKE n` top left all the time, and large in
  the middle for 1.6 s or until the first freeze.
- The room changes inside one world. No map is loaded.
- Reaching the gate: the game pauses for real and offers 3 upgrades the run does not hold. Keys 1, 2,
  3 or a click on a card pick one. Then the next room.
- The last room's gate: the wrap screen with takes, time, shots, freezes and kills. Any key starts a
  new run at take 1.
- Death: after 1.6 s the run starts again at room one as the next take, with no upgrades.
- Health and the rounds in the revolver carry from room to room. Charges refill.

Dev switches (not in Shipping builds):

- `-SupercutRoom=<name>` plays one room as a run of its own.
- `-SupercutRun=<name>` plays `Content\Runs\<name>.txt`.
- `-SupercutSeed=<n>` fixes which upgrades are offered. Without it each start differs.

Log lines (all `LogSupercut`):

## Part C. Code plates, `order=`, `-SupercutUpgrades`, the eight-room main run

Commit PARTC_COMMIT in `D:\UE\Projects\Supercut59`, branch `ue59`, on its own after Part B's `3ddae59`.

### What works

- **A plate that is hit is entered:** its rim lights white, `button_press` plays at the stand and the log says
  `PLATES door <id>: <symbol> entered, n of m`. A hit on an entered plate does nothing (no sound, no log).
- **The stand answers once,** when as many plates are entered as the code is long. In the code's order: every
  plate green, the door opens for good (`door_unlock`, from the door), `... is the code`. Otherwise: every plate
  red for 0.5 s of scene time, all clear, `door_wrong`, `... is wrong, the plates clear`. Before that moment a
  right plate and a wrong one look and sound the same (a test compares the rim colours).
- **Released shots are held per freeze.** A plate hit from a shot that hung (`GetHungInFreeze() > 0`) waits in a
  batch for its freeze. The batch counts, in firing order, once no player shot of that freeze still flies
  (all spent or destroyed), or `PlateReleaseHold` = 0.6 s of scene time (`SupercutTuning.h`) after its first
  hit. The log says which: `the release of freeze n is over (every shot landed or gone | held long enough,
  t s), k plate hits count`. Live shots count on impact, sorted by firing order within the frame as before.
  DOUBLE EXPOSURE twins carry their shot's freeze, so they join its batch; the twin's hit is a second hit on an
  entered plate and does nothing.
- **`order=`** on a `plates` line: four different symbols, left to right, holding every code symbol. Anything
  else refuses the line with a file:line error. Without it the plates mix as before. Documented in
  `lanes\run\HANDOFF.md` section 1, with the new plate rules. The reader got `FSupercutPieceReader::Has(Key)`
  for a setting a piece may leave out.
- **`-SupercutUpgrades=<name>,<name>`** (not in Shipping): every take starts holding these, granted after the
  take's reset so a death keeps them. The names are the keys `PICK taken` prints. An unknown name stops the game
  at `USupercutRun::Grant`'s check. `Tools\run_demo.ps1 -Upgrades doubleexposure,longtake` passes it.
- **`Content\Runs\main.txt` is the eight rooms of `main8.txt`.** The old three are `demo3.txt`. `Script\run.txt`,
  `run_death.txt`, `sound_upgrade.txt` and `demo.txt` say `-Run demo3` in their headers. `main8.txt` stays.
  No automation test named the main run's rooms; `EveryRoomFileAndRunListInContentIsGood` reads both lists.
